articles.title: Supplemental Breast Cancer Screening with Contrast-enhanced Mammography or Abbreviated MRI for Extremely Dense Breasts: The DENSE-2 Trial.
articles.abstract: Women with extremely dense breasts have an increased risk of breast cancer but also a decreased sensitivity of mammography. The Dense Tissue and Early Breast Neoplasm Screening (DENSE) trial, initiated in 2011, showed that supplemental full-protocol MRI screening reduced the number of interval cancers in women with extremely dense breasts. Cost-effective screening scenarios have been described, but imaging costs and capacity remain barriers to implementing full-protocol MRI in population-based breast cancer screening programs. Therefore, the DENSE-2 trial was set up to investigate two alternate screening techniques, contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) or abbreviated MRI (AB-MRI), that are expected to be cheaper and to make more efficient use of the available capacity while potentially achieving similar results to full-protocol MRI. DENSE-2 is a multicenter randomized controlled trial embedded in the Dutch screening program. It comprises two consecutive screening rounds in which women receive the same breast imaging technique both times. The trial investigates the value of supplemental screening with CEM or AB-MRI in women with extremely dense breasts with a negative screening mammogram. The primary aim is to determine whether these methods will lead to a reduction of interval cancers compared with mammography. The DENSE-2 trial results will provide insights into the performance, feasibility, and acceptability of both screening modalities, enable long-term outcome modeling, and support decision-making on the most appropriate screening strategy for women with extremely dense breasts. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06636370 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Bahl in this issue.

articles.title: Mind the Gap: A survey of chronic wound datasets, methods, and clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, venous ulcers, arterial ulcers and pressure ulcers, represent a growing global health challenge with significant morbidity, mortality, and economic burden. Advancements in medical image analysis have shown promise in automating wound detection, segmentation, and measurement. However, translation of these research advances into clinical practice through mobile applications remains limited. This survey presents systematic analysis of the relationship between chronic wound datasets, deep learning methods, and mobile wound assessment applications. We analyse 20 datasets (14 public/partially public and 6 private), including iterative challenge datasets that extend image pool through synthetic augmentation. We review 50 deep learning methods spanning encoder-decoder architectures to self-supervised learning approaches, and evaluate 13 mobile applications (commercially deployed clinical tools and research prototypes). We examine the alignment between publicly available chronic wound datasets and the documented capabilities of mobile wound assessment mobile applications. Our analysis reveals critical misalignments between datasets, algorithms and mobile applications. Existing datasets are typically designed for algorithm benchmarking rather than clinical deployment, and therefore lack standardised acquisition protocols, scale calibration markers, depth information, detailed tissue composition annotations, and representation of diverse skin types. Conversely, reviewed mobile applications report capabilities, including automatic tissue classification, calibrated wound measurement and depth estimation, for which publicly available data is insufficient. We map documented dataset characteristics to capabilities reported among reviewed mobile applications, identify unresolved methodological challenges, and outline key priorities for the field. Based on these insights, we propose actionable recommendations for developing clinically translatable computer vision system for wound assessment. This survey is intended to serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to bridge the gap between medical imaging methodologies and practical demands of clinical wound care.

articles.title: Restaging the primary tumor in localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma after systemic therapy: a scoping review of the role of CT, FDG-PET, and CA19-9.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The introduction of improved multi-agent systemic therapies has made restaging and treatment response assessment in patients with localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) increasingly complex. This scoping review aims to assess and compare methods for local disease restaging and treatment response assessment in localized PDAC, with a focus on their association with resectability, overall survival (OS), and R0-resection rates. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This scoping review included studies on restaging in patients with PDAC following systemic therapy using CT and PET/CT from MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL. RESULTS: Among 4680 identified studies, 20 fulfilled the eligibility criteria. Most (n = 15) studies analyzed CT, and 5 analyzed PET/CT. Groups of restaging methods included new response categories, size-based metrics, volume, vascular contact, tumor attenuation, fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/CT derived metabolic parameters, and resectability criteria. Dual-energy CT-derived extracellular volume (DECT-ECV) was evaluated as a baseline predictive biomarker. Associations between restaging methods and outcomes were reported inconsistently: some studies found significant associations for specific methods, whereas others did not. No restaging method showed a consistent association with both R0-resection and survival across all studies. CONCLUSION: Restaging of localized PDAC after systemic treatment remains challenging due to the limited accuracy of RECIST 1.1, particularly for the classifications partial response and stable disease. The current evidence suggests that integrating additional imaging features, alternative imaging modalities, and the biomarker carbohydrate antigen (CA)19-9 may improve the assessment of resectability and prognosis. These findings support a future version of RECIST 1.1 to alert clinicians to this issue. KEY POINTS: Question How effective are current (PET/)CT-based restaging methods in assessing local disease resectability and prognosis in localized PDAC after modern multi-agent systemic therapy? Findings Current restaging methods show inconsistent association with R0-resection and survival; RECIST 1.1 is particularly limited for the assessment of partial response and stable disease. Clinical relevance Current evidence confirms a need to integrate additional imaging features and the biomarker CA19-9, during restaging in patients with localized pancreatic cancer after modern systemic therapy to improve accuracy and reduce the risk of missed treatment options.

HyM2Surv: Hypergraph learning for cross-magnification and microbiome-attentive multimodal survival prediction.
articles.abstract: Survival prediction is a critical task in cancer prognosis assessment. In recent years, deep learning methods based on multimodal data have been widely applied to this task. However, existing studies primarily focus on the integration of whole slide images (WSIs) and genomic data, while the utilization of intratumoral microbiome information remains limited. Meanwhile, current approaches face two limitations: (i) they fail to fully exploit the multi-magnification information of WSIs, limiting the joint representation learning across different resolutions; and (ii) high-magnification pathological features tend to dominate, leading to modality imbalance between pathology and intratumoral microbiome data. In this study, we propose HyM2Surv, a hypergraph-based framework for multi-magnification multimodal survival prediction. Specifically, the model first captures cross-magnification interactions in pathology by leveraging spatial proximity and phenotypic feature similarity. It then constructs dense cross-modal connections by centering on the microbiome and linking it with pathological features across all magnifications, thereby alleviating modality imbalance. Extensive experiments on four TCGA datasets demonstrate that HyM2Surv consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average improvement of 6.10% in terms of C-index. In addition, the proposed model provides interpretable insights by identifying microbiome-pathology interaction regions that are significantly associated with patient prognosis, highlighting its potential clinical application. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/RanSuLab/HyMMSurv.

articles.title: HistoDiffusion++: A generative visual foundation model for histopathology.
articles.abstract: Histopathology image analysis has been revolutionized with the introduction of deep learning. While task-specific models have shown strong performance, they often rely on large annotated datasets that are difficult to obtain in practice. Recent foundation models mitigate this dependency via self-supervised learning and have achieved promising results in discriminative analysis and text generation. However, the tasks requiring image generation capabilities remain underexplored, especially under data-scarce conditions. Hence, we present HistoDiffusion++, a multi-magnification generative visual foundation model for histopathology. We pretrain the model on Histo-7M, a large-scale dataset of 7.4 million patches from 38,373 whole-slide images spanning 33 cancer types and 12 organs/organ systems at multiple magnifications. To improve training efficiency and synthesis quality, we further incorporate a pretrained discriminative foundation model and apply representation alignment as regularization during pretraining. We evaluate HistoDiffusion++ on two tracks: synthetic augmentation and image-to-image translation. For augmentation, our model improves classification and nuclei segmentation performance beyond baseline strategies. For translation, it achieves promising results in virtual staining and artifact restoration. The code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/PengJin95/HistoDiffusion_Plusplus.

articles.title: ROI-informed cross-modal supervised contrastive learning for multimodal depression classification using rs-fMRI and T1-weighted MRI.
articles.abstract: Neuroimaging-based classification of depression-related symptom and diagnostic groups remains challenging because of clinical and neurobiological heterogeneity. Structural MRI and resting-state functional MRI provide complementary information, but most multimodal approaches rely on global fusion and do not incorporate region-level (ROI) information into cross-modal alignment. We propose a two-stage multimodal framework for depression classification based on ROI-informed cross-modal supervised contrastive learning (RCSCL), which does not require explicit ROI-to-ROI correspondence. Utilizing the Schaefer 200 atlas, we extracted ROI tokens using a MedicalNet-pretrained 3D ResNet-18 for structural MRI and a graph attention network for resting-state fMRI. The tokens were aggregated with attention pooling and the resulting modality-level representations were aligned in a shared embedding space using class-conditional supervised contrastive learning. Global features were then fused using self-attention, and the classification model was optimized using focal loss to address class imbalance. The framework was evaluated on an in-house single-center dataset of 500 subjects and the publicly available SRPBS multi-site MDD dataset. In the primary attention-based implementation, RCSCL significantly increased AUC/AUPRC from 0.805/0.326 to 0.855/0.410 in the in-house dataset and from 0.736/0.704 to 0.766/0.744 on SRPBS, numerically exceeding those of all evaluated fusion baselines without RCSCL; extending RCSCL to these backbones produced further but backbone-dependent gains. Hierarchical visualization analyses identified default mode, limbic, and prefrontal regions as recurrently salient, consistent with prior depression neuroimaging findings, although these attention-derived importance values are model-internal indices. These results suggest that ROI-informed multimodal contrastive learning improves class-discriminative representation learning for multimodal depression classification.

articles.title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
articles.abstract: The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.

articles.title: Style-Prior Enhanced-and-Selective Mamba with Class-Oriented Contrastive Learning for Posterior Subcapsular Cataract Grading.
articles.abstract: Posterior subcapsular cataract (PSC) is a leading cause of blindness and vision impairment globally. Precise PSC grading is critical for immediate treatment and opacity progression observation. Recent studies have suggested the great potential of anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) images in objectively investigating the opacities of PSC compared to conventional slit-lamp examinations with clinical features such as average and maximum. However, the irregular morphology and diffuse distribution modeling of its opacities in AS-OCT images present two significant challenges for precise PSC grading, which have not been addressed previously. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Style-Prior Enhanced-and-Selective State Space Model (SPES-SSM), which effectively captures the irregular morphology and diffuse opacity distribution representations by leveraging the potential of SSM and multi-scale convolution concurrently; and then employs the well-designed style-prior enhanced-and-selective representation block to estimate the relative significances of these two representation types via useful clinical feature (e.g., average and maximum) prior exploration of PSC. By stacking SPES-SSM modules, we construct SPES-Mamba for automated PSC grading based on AS-OCT images. To enhance our SPES-Mamba's reliability and further improve its PSC grading results, we design a class-oriented contrastive learning (COCL), which explores the potential of the ranking matrix of label distance from the aspect of class-averaging. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SPES-Mamba and COCL significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of PSC grading results and reliability.

articles.title: Prevalence and predictors of silent vertebral compression fractures using DXA: a UK Biobank Imaging Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Silent vertebral fractures are common but under-recognised. We aimed to estimate the prevalence in an asymptomatic population and to identify demographic and clinical predictors using the UK Biobank data. MATERIALS AND METHODS: DXA spine images from 2446 asymptomatic UK Biobank participants aged 40-79 years were analysed retrospectively. Vertebral fractures were defined as moderate or severe deformities (≥ 25% vertebral height loss). Fractures were identified using an artificial-intelligence-assisted six-point morphometric algorithm with manual correction and radiologist confirmation. Associations with age, sex, bone mineral density (BMD), body mass index (BMI), medication, and back pain were analysed. RESULTS: A total of 2446 participants (mean age 62.0 ± 7.4 years; 1151 men) were analysed. Moderate or severe vertebral fractures were identified in 356 participants (14.6%). Prevalence increased with age, from 9.4% in participants aged 40-49 years to 19.6% in those aged 70-79 years. Fractures were more common in men than women (18.8% vs. 10.8%; adjusted OR 0.51 for women vs. men, 95% CI 0.40-0.66; p < 0.001). BMD and most conventional clinical risk factors had limited predictive value. CONCLUSIONS: Silent vertebral fractures are common in midlife, frequently occur in individuals with normal bone density, and are more prevalent in men. Conventional clinical risk factors have a limited ability to identify affected individuals. KEY POINTS: Question Silent vertebral fractures are frequently overlooked in asymptomatic individuals, and their prevalence and demographic distribution in middle-aged adults are not well-characterised. Findings In a large asymptomatic cohort, vertebral fractures were common, showed male predominance, and were frequently present in individuals without low bone mineral density or recognised clinical risk factors. Clinical relevance Silent vertebral fractures are prevalent in asymptomatic adults and are poorly captured by conventional risk assessment, indicating limitations of current approaches to fracture identification.

articles.title: Beyond the Headlines: What the Evidence Actually Says About Radiology Today and Into the Future.
Association of PET/CT Metabolic Parameters with Histologic Grade of Lung Adenocarcinoma: Implications for Surgical Decisions.
articles.abstract: Background The grading system for invasive lung adenocarcinoma proposed by the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) has been widely validated. However, the association of PET/CT with IASLC grade and its value in clinical decision-making is unknown. Purpose To investigate the association of PET/CT metabolic parameters with IASLC grade and determine the complementary clinical value of PET/CT in optimizing preoperative surgical decision-making in clinical stage IA (cIA) lung adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent preoperative PET/CT and complete resection for cIA lung adenocarcinoma between September 2020 and March 2022. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma. Multivariable Cox models assessed prognostic effects and interactions between maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and surgical strategy. Propensity score matching was used to balance clinicopathologic characteristics across surgical strategies. Results The study included 2789 patients (median age, 62 years [IQR, 55-68 years]; 1574 women). Logistic regression analysis demonstrated a positive interaction between radiologic type and SUVmax (P = .008) in predicting grade 3 adenocarcinoma. Specific cutoff values for pure solid (cutoff of 4.25) and subsolid (cutoff of 2.30) nodules were identified. Positive interactions between SUVmax and surgery were observed exclusively in pure solid nodules (SUVmax-resection extent for overall survival [OS], P = .048; SUVmax-nodal dissection for OS, P = .045). Stratified analyses showed that segmentectomy and limited lymph node dissection were associated with worse outcomes only in hypermetabolic lesions (SUVmax > 4.25; resection extent hazard ratio [HR] for OS, 2.06 [P = .03]; nodal dissection HR for OS, 2.06 [P = .005]). SUVmax maintained robust predictive efficacy for grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma in the external cohort (area under the receiver operating curve, 0.72 for pure solid nodules and 0.74 for subsolid nodules). Conclusion In patients who underwent PET/CT and complete resection for clinical stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, maximum standardized uptake value was an independent predictor of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma and helped identify high-risk patients treated with segmentectomy or limited nodal dissection. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Myocardial T1 Mapping at 3 T: A Comparison of MOLLI and ShMOLLI across Healthy Volunteers and Various Cardiovascular Pathologies.
articles.abstract: Background The clinical utility of quantitative T1 mapping in cardiac MRI is constrained by variability across acquisition protocols, and a comprehensive comparison between commonly used sequences remains unavailable. Purpose To provide a full range of cardiac MRI native T1 and extracellular volume fraction (ECV) values at 3 T in healthy Chinese adults and participants with various cardiovascular diseases and, as a secondary aim, to establish the relationship between modified Look-Locker inversion recovery (MOLLI) and shortened MOLLI (ShMOLLI) measurements. Materials and Methods This prospective study included healthy volunteers, participants with normal cardiac MRI findings, and participants representing 13 cardiovascular conditions. All participants underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences during a single examination. Global native T1 and ECV values were quantified and compared between sequences and across disease groups. Statistical approaches included t tests, Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen D standardization. Results This study included 1237 clinical participants (mean age ± SD: 51 years ± 14.8; 854 men). Reference values (adjusted mean ± SE) in healthy volunteers were 1170 msec ± 9 (MOLLI) and 1135 msec ± 10 (ShMOLLI) for native T1 and were 24.8% ± 0.6 (both MOLLI and ShMOLLI) for ECV, with women showing higher native T1 values than men (all P ≤ .002). MOLLI yielded systematically higher native T1 than ShMOLLI across all conditions (mean difference: 46.0 msec ± 27.2; all P < .01), whereas ECV did not differ for most conditions (10 of 15 groups; P > .05). Strong intersequence correlations were observed for native T1 (Pearson r = 0.93; P < .001) and ECV (r = 0.95; P < .001). After standardization to sequence-specific baselines, pathologic deviations were comparable between sequences (Cohen D differences ≤0.5 in most groups). A supplementary swine study supported the technical validity of both sequences (r = 0.87-0.90; P < .001). Conclusion In participants who underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences, native T1 was higher with MOLLI than ShMOLLI, but ECV was consistent across sequences. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Dacher and Cadour in this issue.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for Prostate Cancer Detection and Screening on MRI in Global Populations: The SCARLET-1 Study.
articles.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have demonstrated non-inferiority to radiologists for prostate cancer detection on MRI, but evidence in global diagnostic and population-based screening settings remains limited. Purpose To determine whether an AI system can achieve diagnostic performance comparable to radiology readings for detecting Gleason grade group ≥2 prostate cancer on MRI in external diagnostic and screening datasets. Materials and Methods In the SCARLET-1 retrospective validation study, prostate MRIs from adults with suspected prostate cancer (January 2012-October 2024) were used to evaluate an AI system, with external testing in diagnostic (PRIME) and organized screening settings (STHLM3-MRI and IP1-PROSTAGRAM). The primary outcome was agreement between AI assessments and standard-of-care diagnoses of Gleason grade group ≥2 cancer, with diagnostic interchangeability defined relative to the estimated agreement of an average radiologist. Secondary outcomes included area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across datasets and subgroups. Results 22,445 examinations (21,252 male patients; median age, 66 years [IQR 60-71]) were included: 20,471 prostate MRI examinations (19,278 patients; 26 cities, 14 countries) for AI training and internal testing, and 1974 patients (20 external cities, 12 countries) for external testing. External AUCs were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.83, 0.90) in PRIME, 0.89 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.92) in STHLM3-MRI, and 0.84 (95% CI: 0.70, 0.95) in IP1-PROSTAGRAM. The primary outcome was 83.0% (395 of 476; adjusted 95% CI: 78.8%, 87.0%), 87.9% (974 of 1108; adjusted 95% CI: 85.6%, 90.3%), and 87.7% (342 of 390; adjusted 95% CI: 83.6%, 91.5%), respectively, meeting prespecified interchangeability criteria in all datasets. Subgroup performance was consistent across age, risk, cancer location and ethnicity (mean ΔAUC, 0.02), but varied substantially across 25 sites (28% with AUC<0.80; 32% with AUC ≥0.90) and by image quality (AUC, 0.78-0.88). Conclusion AI demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of radiology readings across external diagnostic and screening datasets. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license.

articles.title: Association of Disproportionately Enlarged Subarachnoid Space Hydrocephalus Features at MRI with Cognitive Decline.
articles.abstract: Background The prevalence of incomplete disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space hydrocephalus (DESH) and its cognitive relevance remain unclear. Purpose To determine the prevalence of complete and incomplete DESH and their associations with baseline cognitive impairment and follow-up cognitive decline. Materials and Methods This prospective community-based cohort (age ≥ 65 years) included participants who underwent baseline brain MRI and were followed for 5-7 years. Two radiologists assessed baseline MRI scans for core DESH features: Evans index greater than 0.3, enlargement of the Sylvian fissures (ESF), and tightness of the high-convexity sulci (THC). Complete DESH was defined as all three core features, incomplete DESH as one or two core features, and no DESH as zero core features. Feature combinations were modeled as single binary indicators of copresence (eg, THC plus ESF was 1 if both were present and 0 otherwise). Separate cross-sectional and longitudinal logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations of baseline imaging features with concurrent cognitive impairment and follow-up cognitive decline, respectively. Longitudinal models were fitted separately in participants with normal cognition and in a combined cohort of participants with normal cognition or mild cognitive impairment at baseline. Results Among 2133 participants (median age, 69 years [IQR, 67-73 years]; 1304 female participants), complete DESH, incomplete DESH, and no DESH were present in 37 (1.7%), 988 (46.3%), and 1108 (51.9%), respectively. There was no evidence of an association between baseline imaging features and baseline cognitive impairment (all Holm-adjusted P > .05). Baseline THC was associated with follow-up cognitive decline in the cognitively normal cohort (odds ratio [OR], 2.95 [95% CI: 1.95, 4.45]; Holm-adjusted P < .001) and in the combined cohort (OR, 2.87 [95% CI: 1.96, 4.21]; Holm-adjusted P < .001). THC plus ESF was associated with decline only in the combined cohort (OR, 1.83 [95% CI: 1.16, 2.87]; Holm-adjusted P = .04). Conclusion Incomplete DESH was more prevalent than complete DESH. Baseline THC was associated with subsequent cognitive decline. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Haller in this issue.

articles.title: Towards scalable cancer prognosis by aligning semi-supervised learning with survival modeling.
articles.abstract: Prognostic assessment via whole-slide images (WSIs) is a key task in computational pathology. However, the development of robust predictive models is often bottlenecked by the scarcity of survival-annotated data, given the longitudinal nature of clinical follow-up. Despite its potential, semi-supervised learning (SSL) remains underexplored in this field. Existing SSL methods, primarily designed for natural image classification, rely on the assumption of marginally independent categories, which makes them difficult to adapt to the high-dimensional complexity of WSIs and the temporal continuity inherent in survival outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel semi-supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework tailored for WSI-based prognosis. Specifically, we first introduce a morphology-perceived MIL network (Morph-MIL) that jointly models tissue composition and global semantic representations. To maintain a stable reference, a dynamic memory bank is employed to encapsulate the multi-level representations of labeled samples (censored & uncensored). Furthermore, we develop a pseudo-labeling strategy that assigns discrete labels containing temporal relationships to annotation-free data by aligning their features with the memory bank through bin-wise aggregation. Comprehensive evaluation establishes the superiority of the proposed framework, while extensive ablation analyses and visualizations confirm its efficacy in prognostic prediction and biological interpretation. Consequently, this study offers a scalable solution for WSI survival modeling in scenarios with limited annotations. The code is available at: https://github.com/yihuangswust-alt/SSL-Morph_MIL.

articles.title: Quantitative and qualitative magnetic resonance imaging-based analysis to predict postoperative disease progression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common abdominal malignancies and the third leading cause of cancer-related death globally. Predicting the postoperative prognosis of HCC remains an important area of clinical research. Many qualitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) indicators have been used for noninvasive and global assessment of HCC for diagnostic and prognostic purposes. However, the prognostic value of quantitative MRI parameters has not been extensively validated in multicenter cohorts. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to verify whether MRI-based imaging features could improve prognostic prediction in patients with HCC. We developed prognostic models to predict the progression-free survival (PFS) of patients with HCC. METHODS: In this multicenter cohort study, 203 patients diagnosed with early- to intermediate-stage HCC were divided into a training dataset and an external validation dataset. In addition to clinical indicators, the candidates included qualitative and quantitative MRI data. Three noninvasive models were developed: the Clinical Model, the Radiological Model, and the Combined Model. The patients were stratified according to the risk of disease progression. Model performance was assessed through discrimination and calibration analyses, decision curve analysis was performed, and a clinical application was designed. In addition, the subgroups at different stages of the disease were analyzed, and PFS was compared between the high- and low-risk groups. RESULTS: Prognostic nutritional index, tumor-feeding vessels, mosaic architecture and the signal enhancement ratio (SER) parameter were identified as independent predictors of disease progression in patients with HCC. The Combined Model demonstrated superior performance compared with the Clinical and Radiological Models. The areas under the curve (AUCs) in the training dataset were 0.822, 0.748, and 0.795, whereas those in the validation dataset were 0.819, 0.758, and 0.677, respectively. The Combined Model also demonstrated favorable calibration and greater net clinical benefit on decision curve analysis. Its predictive ability remained consistent regardless of the Child-Pugh classification or Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the important role of quantitative and qualitative MRI assessments in evaluating the prognosis of patients with HCC and emphasizes the predictive value of SER parameter. However, these findings should nevertheless be interpreted with caution given the relatively limited sample size, despite the use of bootstrap internal validation and external validation.

Concept-Based Explainable AI in Retinal Imaging: Core Concepts, Techniques, and Challenges.
articles.abstract: In high-stakes domains like healthcare, establishing trust in AI-assisted decisions is critical for fostering confidence among experts and researchers. However, standard explanation methods may not fully meet clinical needs, offering raw data, such as saliency maps, rather than human-readable text and auditable, transparent reasoning. To bridge this gap, researchers are increasingly adopting concept-based approaches that express model reasoning through human-readable concepts grounded in expert-backed clinical knowledge. Although this field has advanced rapidly in recent years, retinal C-XAI remains methodologically heterogeneous, with limited agreement on taxonomy, evaluation, and clinical validation. This review identifies recurring reliability gaps in retinal C-XAI and synthesises potential directions for addressing them, including independent concept-level auditing, robustness testing, and clinician-informed validation. As an illustrative example, we discuss how the established SMILE methodology could be adapted for concept-level auditing in retinal C-XAI; this is presented as a candidate research direction rather than a new or clinically validated framework.

articles.title: Clinical Usability Evaluation of CT Work Systems: A Narrative Review and Socio-Technical Implementation Framework.
articles.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) services are commonly evaluated using image quality, radiation dose, and equipment uptime. These metrics, however, do not establish whether CT work systems can be used safely, efficiently, and consistently across clinical information flows. This review synthesizes usability standards, human factors concepts, and radiology informatics evidence to support clinical evaluation of CT work systems. The scope included scanner interfaces, RIS/PACS/EMR links, dose monitoring tools, protocol repositories, and workflow logs. We conducted a transparent narrative review using targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and IEEE Xplore searches, Crossref metadata checks, standards, guidance documents, and citation chaining. Evidence was organized by context of use, information system component, risk-relevant task, evaluation method, and implementation action. CT usability is a socio-technical property linking users, tasks, scanner interfaces, information systems, protocol governance, maintenance, and organizational context. No single method captures this system adequately. Digital timestamps and observation reveal workflow delays, while task-based testing and scales characterize interface performance and user burden. Protocol, dose monitoring, and maintenance audits identify lifecycle risks. The proposed framework maps five domains to evaluation methods, candidate indicators, mitigation strategies, and minimum reporting items. Comprehensive CT usability assessment should extend beyond global satisfaction and equipment performance. It should determine whether specified users can complete defined CT tasks within defined clinical and informatics contexts. Future research should validate CT-specific task libraries, usability scales, interoperable log definitions, and multi-site reporting standards.

articles.title: Use of Machine Learning and Imaging to Predict Outcomes After Lumbar Spine Surgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Postoperative outcomes following lumbar spine surgery remain variable, and existing clinical risk stratification methods offer limited predictive accuracy. Advances in machine learning enable quantitative analysis of routinely acquired spinal imaging, creating opportunities to improve preoperative outcome prediction. However, the methodological quality and clinical readiness of imaging-based machine learning models in lumbar spine surgery have not been systematically evaluated. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through October 2025 for studies using machine learning models trained on imaging data (MRI, CT, or radiographs) to predict postoperative outcomes after lumbar spine surgery. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST). Twenty-six studies published between 2019 and 2025 met inclusion criteria. Most models predicted patient-reported or clinical outcomes, with fewer addressing complications, structural outcomes, or imaging-derived biomarkers. MRI was the predominant modality. Model discrimination was frequently moderate to high (median AUC, 0.83), though external validation and calibration reporting were uncommon. All studies demonstrated high risk of bias, primarily related to analysis and validation practices. Imaging-based machine learning models show promise for improving preoperative outcome prediction after lumbar spine surgery, but methodological limitations limit current clinical applicability. Greater emphasis on external validation, standardized outcomes, and prospective evaluation is needed to support safe translation into routine spine care.

articles.title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics.
articles.abstract: The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.

articles.title: Foundation Models and Multimodal Learning for Medical Data with Applications in Oncology.
articles.abstract: The rapid expansion of medical data, including radiological imaging, digital pathology, molecular profiling, electronic health records, and longitudinal clinical narratives, has created new opportunities for AI in healthcare, while also exposing the limitations of traditional unimodal modeling approaches. Multimodal learning addresses these challenges by integrating heterogeneous data sources, and recent advances in foundation models, large-scale pretrained models designed for broad task transfer, have further accelerated this shift. Together, these developments have given rise to multimodal foundation models that aim to learn generalizable, aligned representations across diverse clinical modalities. In this review, we provide an overview of multimodal foundation models in medical AI, with a particular focus on oncology. We first outline key medical data modalities and the machine learning objectives that motivate multimodal integration, including predictive, representational, and alignment-based goals. We then examine core architectural design patterns and training paradigms underlying multimodal foundation models, such as modality-specific encoders, fusion strategies, attention mechanisms, contrastive pretraining, and scalable self-supervised learning. Building on this foundation, we survey representative multimodal models across radiology, pathology, clinical text, and molecular domains. We further review applications of multimodal foundation models across the cancer care continuum, including early detection, diagnosis and subtyping, prognosis, therapy response prediction, and longitudinal survival modeling. Finally, we discuss critical challenges that limit clinical translation, including cross-institutional heterogeneity, temporal misalignment across modalities, weak supervision, interpretability, regulatory constraints, and workflow integration, and outline future directions for advancing safe and effective deployment in real-world oncology practice.

articles.title: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations in Radiology and Medical Imaging Education: Educational Effectiveness, Validity, and Implementation-A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To synthesize evidence on objective structured clinical examinations (OSCEs) in radiology and medical imaging education, focusing on educational outcomes, validity evidence, reliability, scoring, feasibility, and implementation consequences. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, ERIC, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to July 20, 2026. Eligibility was limited to radiology, radiography, nuclear medicine, sonography, and medical student imaging curricula; clinician bedside POCUS courses outside radiology or medical imaging education were excluded. Educational-effect studies were appraised with MERSQI. Measurement evidence was appraised across seven validity and implementation domains. Meta-analysis was considered only for sufficiently comparable independent studies. RESULTS: Forty-three reports met the narrowed scope: 22 measurement/implementation reports and 21 educational-effect reports. Educational studies comprised six randomized studies, nine nonrandomized comparisons, one pre-post study, and five post-course or implementation studies. Seven reports favored the intervention, one met a noninferiority criterion, one was mixed, six were uncertain, and six were not estimable as comparative effects. MERSQI scores ranged from 10.5 to 14.0. Feasibility was documented in all measurement reports, but internal-structure or reliability evidence was absent in ten, and consequence evidence was strong in only one. CONCLUSION: Imaging-focused OSCEs are feasible and useful for local assessment in radiology and medical imaging education, but evidence remains heterogeneous and incompletely supported by reliability, response-process, and consequence data.

articles.title: Abbreviated MRI and Ultrafast MRI of the Breast.
articles.abstract: Detection of breast cancer in MRI requires fast, dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) imaging covering the immediate post-contrast phase, that is, the first 60 s after contrast injection. This ensures selective depiction of invasive cancer as well as DCIS against an otherwise dark background, that is, before background parenchymal enhancement (BPE) can set in. Thus, breast MRI requires not only high spatial, but also high temporal resolution. Both, abbreviated breast MRI (AB-MRI) as well as ultrafast breast MRI (UF-MRI), exploit the fact that enhancement of cancers versus their non-cancerous background differs most in the immediate post-contrast phase. Beyond this, however, AB-MRI and UF-MRI are unrelated: AB-MRI is a novel MRI paradigm; UF-MRI is a novel MRI pulse sequence that allows time-resolved imaging of the immediate post-contrast phase. AB-MRI is an umbrella term for lean, streamlined MRI protocols designed to answer specific clinical questions. Compared with "all-purpose" full-protocol MRI, AB-MRI allows a substantial reduction of acquisition time. The first proposed use case of AB-MRI was for breast cancer screening, to reduce cost, and thus improve access and tolerability. It had been termed "FAST," short for "first post-contrast subtracted imaging," because it truncated the breast MRI acquisition protocol after one post-contrast scan covering the immediate post-contrast phase. Around the same time, UF-MRI was inaugurated. This may have caused the misunderstanding that both would represent different positions on the same line of development, with "ultrafast" being even faster than "FAST." AB-MRI protocols can be categorized into short and abridged protocols. Short protocols concentrate on the pre- and immediate post-contrast phase, either by regular DCE-MRI, or by UF-MRI. Abridged protocols add carefully selected scans, for example, T2-weighted and/or post-contrast scans. This review aims at clarifying the definitions and respective concepts of AB-MRI and UF-MRI, and to summarize the current evidence regarding the respective utility for breast cancer diagnosis.

articles.title: Virtual Noncontrast Lung Densitometry with Photon-counting CT: The Importance of Breathing-An Early Career Perspective.
Colour maps for representation of quantitative metrics in radiology: meaningful or misleading?
articles.abstract: The increased utility of quantitative metrics in medical imaging has prompted the use of colour representation of the data. Colour schemes for image display can highlight pathology and distinguish normal anatomy, thus potentially aiding image interpretation. Adding colour schemes to images may serve the sole purpose of visualising an abnormality or may seek to represent and meaningfully convey a quantitative metric. An early use of colour representation is exemplified by colour Doppler in ultrasound (US), where a two-sided linear scale is commonly applied. More recently, many schemes have arisen, ranging from a single colour to depict a segmented region to a range of colours that embrace the entire colour spectrum. These may be applied as continuous or discrete palettes, depending on the software vendor or even on individual user settings. The lack of standardisation of colour schemes across the medical community, especially in medical imaging, risks misinterpretation of quantitative data and potential unintended negative clinical consequences. The purpose of this article is to review the colour schemes used for quantitative imaging across US, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography (PET), the way in which they are applied, the clinical applications where their use is desirable for enhanced interpretation, and the pitfalls where standardisation is lacking in a variety of clinical applications. Finally, we discuss some solutions that could be employed to enable standardisation and augment the use of colour in image interpretation. KEY POINTS: Question Colour schemes in medical imaging can highlight pathology, but standardisation is lacking for most imaging modalities, thus risking misinterpretation of quantitative data. Findings For T1, T2, and T2* maps and their inverses, colour map recommendations have recently been proposed, but are mostly lacking for other quantitative data. Critical relevance statement Standardised colour maps can enhance data analyses across scanners and institutions, which is important for multicentre studies and handling big data. Furthermore, standardised and harmonised colour maps could improve lesion conspicuity, cross-platform comparability, and longitudinal reliability.

articles.title: Adult diagnostic reference levels in computed tomography: A systematic review and analysis of regional variability.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT) is vital in diagnostic imaging but involves ionizing radiation, requiring careful dose management. Diagnostic Reference Levels (DRLs), recommended by the International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP), serve as benchmarks for optimizing radiation doses and improving patient safety. While many DRL studies exist, most focus on individual countries, anatomical regions, or clinical indications, limiting broader applicability. This systematic review addresses this gap by analyzing adult CT DRLs across continents and major anatomical areas. It compares international benchmarks, highlights methodological inconsistencies, and explores drivers of regional variability to inform global dose optimization. METHODS: Following PRISMA-S guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase identified studies published in English from 2018 to 2025. Keywords related to DRLs and CT imaging were used. Studies reporting DRLs for adult CT using standardized dose metrics were included. Pediatric studies, narrative reviews, Phantom studies, case reports, pilot studies, and gray literature were excluded. RESULTS: Of 2719 identified articles, 63 met the inclusion criteria. Local DRLs were reported in 48 % of studies, and national DRLs in 52 %. Substantial variability was observed across examination types and geographical regions. For head CT, CTDIvol values ranged from 38.2 to 117.6 mGy, while DLP values ranged from 512 to 1943 mGy·cm across the included studies. Similar variability was observed for other examination categories, which may reflect differences in patient characteristics, equipment, and imaging protocols. CONCLUSION: This systematic review identified substantial international variability in DRLs for adult CT examinations, associated with differences in imaging practices, patient characteristics, available technology, and methodological approaches to DRL establishment. The 75th percentile was the most commonly used method for defining DRLs across the included studies. These findings support regular DRL review and greater methodological standardization to improve comparability across regions and strengthen CT dose optimization practices.

articles.title: Rotating Frame Spin-Lock Cardiac MRI Method at 9.4 T Can Characterize Diffuse Fibrosis in Progressing Hypertensive Heart Disease in Mice.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the applicability of rotating frame spin-lock continuous wave (CW) T1ρ and relaxation along a fictitious field with Rank 2 (RAFF2) methods complementary to native T1 and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) for cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) of diffuse fibrosis in mice with advancing hypertensive heart disease (HHD) and diastolic dysfunction. METHODS: HHD was induced in mice with angiotensin II infusion for 28 days; sham operated were used as controls. Phenotype progression was assessed with echocardiography. Characterization of diffuse fibrosis was performed with CMRI. CW-T1ρ and RAFF2 were compared with native T1 and LGE acquired on Days 14 and 28 of the experiment. Regions of interest in CMRI relaxation time maps and Picrosirius red-stained histological cardiac sections were compared. RESULTS: Diffuse fibrosis in the left ventricle was visible on Day 14 with TRAFF2 relaxation time maps in the HHD group with early diastolic impairment, and CW-T1ρ showed a slight increase. Both CW-T1ρ and TRAFF2 showed elevated values on Day 28 in HHD mice, whereas native T1 showed an increase only on Day 28. LGE showed no accumulation. The presence of diffuse fibrosis was verified with cardiac histology. CONCLUSIONS: Rotating frame spin-lock CW-T1ρ and RAFF2 are more sensitive to native T1 and LGE in the characterization of diffuse fibrosis in advancing HHD in mice, being an alternative for the imaging of fibrotic remodeling also in other cardiac pathologies.

articles.title: A rare case of bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions.
articles.abstract: Cuboid-navicular coalitions are an exceptionally rare form of tarsal coalitions, representing less than 1% of all tarsal coalitions. Although tarsal coalitions classically become symptomatic during adolescence, cuboid-navicular coalitions may remain clinically silent until adulthood and can present with nonspecific chronic midfoot or hindfoot pain. We present a rare case of bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions in a 42-year-old man with progressive bilateral midfoot pain, associated degenerative hindfoot and midfoot changes, and bilateral peroneal tendon pathology. Initial management consisted of orthotics, bracing, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but symptoms progressed over 8 years. Cross-sectional imaging demonstrated bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions, progressive degenerative changes, and high-grade right peroneus longus tear. The patient underwent excision of the right cuboid-navicular coalition, excision of the right lateral calcaneal tubercle with inferior peroneal retinacular release, and debridement and repair of the right peroneus longus and brevis tendons. This case highlights the importance of considering rare tarsal coalitions in adults with chronic nonspecific midfoot pain and emphasizes the value of MRI and CT for diagnosis, characterization of associated pathology, and operative planning.

articles.title: Development and Prospective Validation of an Interpretable Machine Learning Model Integrating Cardiac MRI Extracellular Volume for 1-Year MACE Prediction Post-STEMI.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Extracellular volume (ECV) quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is a key indicator of myocardial fibrosis and strongly linked to outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). This research focused on the development and validation of an interpretable machine learning (ML) model that incorporates ECV to predict 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in patients with STEMI following percutaneous coronary intervention. MATERIALS AND METHODS: MACE prediction models were developed using clinical variables combined with CMR-ECV parameters and validated in a prospective cohort. Feature selection was conducted through Boruta algorithms and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithms, and eight ML algorithms were trained. Model performance was assessed by discrimination and calibration. The top performer was interpreted by Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. An interactive online nomogram was deployed to facilitate personalized perioperative risk management. RESULTS: Among 673 STEMI patients (derivation: n = 398; prospective validation: n = 275), five key predictors were identified: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), myocardial infarction ECV (MI-ECV), age, and creatine kinase-MB. The random forest model achieved the highest discriminative performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.825, 95% confidence interval: 0.763-0.876). SHAP analysis identified NT-proBNP as the most impactful feature, with LVEF class and MI-ECV ranking next. CONCLUSION: Integration of CMR-derived ECV into an interpretable machine learning framework enables accurate 1-year MACE risk prediction following STEMI. This approach combines robust discriminative performance with clinical transparency through SHAP-based explanations, offering a proof-of-concept tool for precision cardiovascular care.

articles.title: Generalizability of Deep Learning Architectures for Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Classification in Histopathology: A Comparative CNN-Vision Transformer Study with External Validation and Label-Quality Analysis.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent oral malignancy, with delayed diagnosis contributing to poor survival. Deep learning has shown promise for histopathological detection of OSCC, but reported performance is frequently based on single-source datasets, with limited external validation and variable annotation quality. Our study was to compare representative CNN and transformer architectures for histopathological OSCC classification and assess their generalizability under external domain shift. A total of 10,817 H&E-stained image patches from 114 patients were classified as OSCC or normal/control. Images were independently reviewed by two oral pathologists, with discordant cases adjudicated by a senior pathologist (Cohen's κ = 0.975). Eight ImageNet-pre-trained architectures (ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T) were fine-tuned using three random seeds. Models were trained, validated, and tested on the internally curated dataset {MIDAS} and subsequently evaluated on two independent external datasets used exclusively for external validation. Diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, statistical significance, and model interpretability were assessed. To investigate the observed reduction in external performance, cancer-labelled images from the external datasets underwent post hoc expert pathological review for potential label discordance. A total of 10,817 H&E-stained image patches from 114 patients were classified as OSCC or normal/control. Images were independently reviewed by two oral pathologists, with discordant cases adjudicated by a senior pathologist (Cohen's κ = 0.975). Eight ImageNet-pre-trained architectures (ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T) were fine-tuned using three random seeds. Models were evaluated on a patient-level internal test set and two independent external datasets. Diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, statistical differences, and interpretability were assessed. Cancer-labelled images from External Dataset 2 were post hoc reassessed for label discordance. ConvNeXt-Tiny demonstrated the strongest overall performance. Substantial external degradation across models highlights the effects of domain shift and label quality, emphasizing expert annotation, independent validation, reproducible benchmarking, and multi-institutional datasets for clinical translation.

articles.title: CSNet: Cognitive Simulation Network for Reliable Histopathology-Based Cancer Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Histopathology-based cancer diagnosis is crucial for early detection and timely therapeutic intervention. However, most deep learning methods for histopathological image classification are mainly optimized as prediction models, with limited consideration of clinical diagnostic workflows. In routine practice, pathologists usually follow a sequential reasoning process: coarse assessment of possible abnormalities, detailed inspection of suspicious regions, and consultation-based reasoning to reduce uncertainty. To provide more reliable and interpretable decision support for histopathology-based cancer diagnosis, we propose the cognitive simulation network (CSNet), which draws inspiration from pathologists' sequential diagnostic workflow. First, the multi-view fuzzy assessment module integrates frequency, texture, and gradient cues through learnable fuzzy membership functions to estimate view-level abnormality degrees, providing an initial assessment of suspicious pathological evidence. Guided by this assessment, the gradient-guided fuzzy modulator converts abnormality information into spatial guidance, enhancing informative high-gradient morphological responses while suppressing redundant low-informative regions. Based on the modulated representations, the uncertainty-guided multi-expert synergy mechanism estimates diagnostic uncertainty and coordinates multiple expert branches to generate consensus representations for reliable prediction. Extensive experiments on Kather-5 K, LC25000, LC25000-clean, and a collected cervical cancer histopathology dataset demonstrate that CSNet achieves superior performance, with accuracies of 97.673%, 99.964%, 97.920%, and 99.861%, respectively. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed designs, and statistical analyses confirm the reliability of the observed improvements. Meanwhile, robustness evaluations and comparative visualizations demonstrate stable performance and more consistent responses in diagnostically relevant tissue regions, highlighting the potential of CSNet for reliable histopathology-based cancer diagnosis.

articles.title: Semi-Automated Image Labeling and Object Tracking for MR-Guided Radiotherapy Using a Foundation Vision Model.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT) enables real-time tracking of tumor and organ motion for more precise radiation delivery. However, existing clinical tracking software struggles with high-velocity or non-rigid motion. Foundation models, such as Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) and MedSAM2, offer robust tracking with fast inference speeds and strong zero-shot accuracy that can improve with fine-tuning. Fine-tuning typically uses expert-labeled datasets, which are expensive to acquire. We explored SAM2's utility in accelerating the labeling process by developing a workflow where novices label < 1% of frames and SAM2 automatically labels the rest. We then evaluated SAM2 and MedSAM2 for tumor tracking on an open-access MRgRT dataset in three configurations: zero-shot, fine-tuned using manually labeled data, and fine-tuned using the semi-automatically labeled data. We measured accuracy with the Dice similarity coefficient, 95th percentile (P95) Hausdorff distance, and centroid distance. MedSAM2 and SAM2 demonstrated strong zero-shot tracking accuracy with no significant difference among the model variants. Fine-tuning significantly improved Dice coefficients (0.874 to 0.891, p = 0.006), P95 Hausdorff distances (9.069 to 4.378 mm, p < 0.001), and centroid distances (5.299 to 1.769 mm, p < 0.001) relative to zero-shot, with no significant difference between using manually labeled and semi-automatically labeled data. Therefore, leveraging SAM2 to semi-automatically generate labeled training data can substantially reduce the cost of data curation and long-term model maintenance without compromising accuracy.

articles.title: From Intra- to Inter-habitat Analysis: Spatial Structure Features for Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis Prediction on Breast DCE-MRI.
articles.abstract: Habitat radiomics characterizes texture within tumor subregions but discards the spatial relationships between them. We developed a landscape-ecology-inspired framework quantifying inter-habitat spatial structure on DCE-MRI, evaluated its complementary value alongside within-habitat radiomics, and compared early versus late fusion, using axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) prediction as the evaluation task. In this multicenter retrospective study, 284 patients from one center were randomly split into training (n = 198) and validation (n = 86) cohorts, with 120 patients from an independent institution as the external test set. Tumors were partitioned into six habitats by k-means clustering of 19 voxel-wise texture descriptors, with centroids derived exclusively from the training cohort. Three feature domains were constructed: 8 clinical parameters, 642 within-habitat radiomics features, and 94 inter-habitat spatial structure features spanning fragmentation (n = 30), morphology (n = 24), inter-habitat contact (n = 15), inter-habitat distance (n = 15), area ratio (n = 6), and diversity (n = 4). In the external test set, progressive fusion yielded incremental gains in AUC: clinical alone 0.754, plus within-habitat radiomics 0.843, plus inter-habitat spatial structure 0.863 (95% CI 0.792-0.934). The full early fusion model achieved higher AUC than the clinical-only (DeLong P = 0.011) and spatial-structure-only models (P = 0.044); early fusion yielded a numerically higher AUC than late fusion without reaching significance (0.863 vs 0.851, P = 0.636). The two single-domain imaging models were statistically indistinguishable (0.817 vs 0.784, P = 0.512). Inter-habitat spatial structure captures tumor organization overlooked by conventional habitat radiomics and provides complementary information for preoperative ALNM prediction.

articles.title: Development and External Testing of an Interpretable MRI-Based Machine Learning Model for Differentiating Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma from Cellular Leiomyoma.
articles.abstract: This retrospective two-center diagnostic study was aimed at developing and externally testing an interpretable MRI-based machine learning model for differentiating endometrial stromal sarcoma (ESS) from cellular leiomyoma (CL). A total of 155 women with pathologically confirmed ESS or CL were assigned to a derivation cohort (n = 111) and an external testing cohort (n = 44). Clinical variables, qualitative MRI features, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) histogram parameters were evaluated. Three MRI-derived predictors-irregular tumor margin, cystic areas on T2-weighted imaging, and mean ADC-were used to train six classifiers. The final support vector machine model with a radial basis function kernel was evaluated at a fixed threshold determined in the derivation cohort using receiver operating characteristic, calibration, decision curve, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analyses. A reader study assessed the effect of model assistance. The model achieved areas under the curve of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.760-0.917) in the derivation cohort and 0.835 (95% CI, 0.669-0.960) in the external testing cohort. Calibration and decision curve analyses indicated acceptable performance and potential clinical utility. In an exploratory model-assisted reader analysis, junior radiologist specificity increased from 46.4 to 82.1% and accuracy from 52.3 to 77.3%. This interpretable three-feature model demonstrated promising performance across cohorts and may serve as an adjunctive tool for preoperative MRI assessment, although prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

articles.title: Interpretable Source-Aware Bone-Muscle Fusion Framework for Multicenter Prediction of Osteoporotic Vertebral Fractures.
articles.abstract: Osteoporotic vertebral fracture (OVF) is underrecognized, and bone mineral density (BMD) alone may be insufficient for prediction. We developed the multisource fusion model for osteoporotic vertebral fracture (MSF-OVF), an interpretable source-aware framework integrating clinical-demographic variables, BMD, and lumbar MRI-derived ventral and dorsal paraspinal muscle (PM) representations. This retrospective multicenter study included 2680 participants aged > 40 years from five centers (one training, one internal validation, four external test cohorts). Deep features from four PM regions were extracted using vision foundation model-guided transfer learning and integrated with age, sex, body mass index, and BMD through source-aware latent fusion. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), calibration, and interpretability analyses. MSF-OVF achieved an AUC of 0.881 (95% CI, 0.854-0.909) in internal validation and 0.851-0.917 across four external cohorts. Compared with the clinical-demographic and BMD baseline, MSF-OVF improved AUC by 0.046-0.093 and significantly outperformed it in internal validation and most external cohorts (DeLong P ≤ 0.034). Continuous NRI was 0.268-1.034 across all validation cohorts (P ≤ 0.011). MSF-OVF also outperformed single-muscle models (AUC, 0.454-0.736; P ≤ 0.009). After training-derived logistic recalibration, the internal validation Brier score was 0.140, with a calibration-in-the-large (CITL) of - 0.168 and calibration slope of 0.926. Class activation maps mainly highlighted PM regions. Automated segmentation took several seconds and inference 57.71 ± 18.66 ms per participant. Source-aware fusion of clinical-demographic, BMD, and PM MRI information may support computer-aided multicenter OVF prediction.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Computed Tomography Classification of Posterior Malleolar Fractures for a Standardized Diagnostic Framework.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in computed tomography (CT)-based classification systems for posterior malleolar fractures (PMFs), diagnostic consistency remains limited because these systems are still highly dependent on the observer's experience. This study aimed to develop a deep learning-based automated model capable of classifying PMFs according to the Haraguchi, Mason-Molloy, and Bartoníček-Rammelt clasification systems using CT scans, and to compare the classification performance of different convolutional neural network architectures. Retrospectively collected preoperative CT data from 480 adult patients with PMFs were analyzed. A total of 2398 CT slices were independently classified by three orthopedic surgeons according to the three classification systems, and majority consensus was used as the reference standard. Anonymized DICOM images were evaluated using VGG-16, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-121 architectures. The dataset was divided into 60% training, 20% validation, and 20% testing subsets. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The VGG-16 and ResNet-101 models demonstrated high classification performance in the Haraguchi and Mason-Molloy systems. In the VGG-16 model, AUC values exceeded 0.90 across most fracture subtypes, reaching particularly high levels in Haraguchi types I-III, Mason-Molloy types IIB and III, and Bartoníček-Rammelt type IV. Similarly, the ResNet-101 model achieved AUC values above 0.90 in most classes, with very high discriminative performance observed in selected subtypes. F1-scores were greater than 0.70 among most fracture categories and exceeded 0.80 in several, indicating strong and consistent classification performance. These findings demonstrate that deep learning-based automated CT classification of PMFs is feasible and diagnostically robust. The proposed framework may improve diagnostic consistency, reduce observer-dependent variability, and support standardized assessment of posterior malleolar fractures in clinical practice.

articles.title: CLIP-CGPNet: A Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for Postoperative UTUC Recurrence Prediction.
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of postoperative recurrence is essential for individualized management and follow-up planning in patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). However, reliable risk stratification remains challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of imaging characteristics and clinical information. In this study, we propose a multimodal clinical decision support framework that integrates contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) images with routinely available clinical variables for postoperative recurrence prediction. The proposed framework adopts an image-clinical integrated learning strategy to enhance semantic alignment between visual representations and patient-specific clinical context. Imaging features are guided by clinically informed semantic prompts, while a dynamic fusion mechanism adaptively balances the contributions of different modalities. This design enables robust multimodal interaction and improves the individualized risk estimation. The framework is evaluated using a retrospective UTUC cohort of 160 patients treated between 2016 and 2023, including 59 recurrence cases and 101 nonrecurrence cases. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.87, demonstrating superior performance compared with conventional convolutional neural network-based models and representative multimodal baselines. Qualitative analyses further indicate improved alignment between imaging patterns and clinical factors, providing interpretable insights through attention-based visualization. These findings suggest that the proposed multimodal framework provides a potential approach for postoperative UTUC recurrence risk stratification and has the potential to support clinical decision-making and risk-adapted postoperative management.

articles.title: Comparison of the Performances of Deep Learning Methods in Kellgren-Lawrence Classification of Knee Osteoarthritis: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) causes symptoms such as pain, stiffness, and functional limitation in the knees; plain knee radiographs are used in addition to physical examination in its diagnosis. This study aimed to compare the performance of pre-trained deep learning models in knee OA classification and to examine the effects of lateral knee radiographs and patient clinical data on the performance of these models. Eight centers participated in the study; radiographs from six centers were used for training, validation, and testing of the models, and radiographs from two centers were used for external validation. In addition to anteroposterior (AP) and lateral knee radiographs, clinical information such as age, gender, height, and weight was collected from the patients. A total of 1550 patients were included in the study. The performance of deep learning models VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, Inception_v3, and EfficientNetb0 was compared in the classification of knee OA. The VGG-16 model yielded significantly higher performance metrics than competing architectures (p < 0.001), with an accuracy of 0.73, sensitivity of 0.72, specificity of 0.93, F1 score of 0.72, positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.72, quadratic weighted Kappa of 0.91, and AUC of 0.93. Feature extraction was performed using the VGG-16 model, and the patient's age, gender, and BMI clinical characteristics were added to the image feature set and classified using machine learning algorithms. The XGBoost classifier showed statistically insignificant improvements of 1-2% in performance metrics. Similar performance results were obtained with the VGG-16 model in a study using only AP knee radiographs. Radiographs from two centers were used for external validation, and the VGG-16 model yielded accuracy of 0.65, sensitivity of 0.65, specificity of 0.91, PPV of 0.67, F1 score of 0.65, quadratic weighted kappa of 0.88, and AUC of 0.90. Adding age, gender, and BMI clinical characteristics to the knee radiograph image feature set did not significantly improve model performance. Furthermore, adding lateral radiographs to the AP knee radiograph set did not provide any additional contribution to KL classification performance.

articles.title: HCF-Net: a Hierarchical Cascade Fusion Network Aligned with Clinical Treatment Pathways for Preoperative Molecular Subtyping of Breast Cancer on Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI.
articles.abstract: Preoperative molecular subtyping of breast cancer is essential for treatment selection and prognosis assessment, yet most deep learning approaches formulate subtype prediction as a conventional flat multi-class task without reflecting the sequential clinical decision process. We developed HCF-Net, a hierarchical cascade fusion network that decomposes subtype prediction into three clinically aligned binary decision nodes and integrates multiphase DCE-MRI with clinicoradiologic information. The model was retrospectively developed and validated using a dual-center cohort of 373 women who underwent preoperative 3.0 T multiphase DCE-MRI. On an independent test set (n = 75), HCF-Net achieved a Macro-AUC of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.806-0.923), accuracy of 73.3%, Macro-F1 of 0.732, and Cohen's κ of 0.631. The fusion model consistently achieved the highest AUC across all three hierarchical decision nodes, reaching 0.890 for luminal versus non-luminal tumors, 0.865 for Luminal A versus Luminal B tumors, and 0.974 for HER2-enriched versus triple-negative tumors. The same ordering of classification strategies was observed with a ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone. Compared with conventional flat classification strategies, hierarchical cascade decomposition and decision-level fusion provided substantial performance gains. These findings suggest that a hierarchical fusion framework aligned with clinical decision pathways may provide an effective and interpretable approach for preoperative breast cancer molecular subtype prediction.

articles.title: Validation of a Deep Learning Model for Automated Ureteral Length Measurement on CT Against Gross Specimens.
articles.abstract: This study validates a deep learning model for automated ureteral length measurement on CT using gross specimen measurements as the reference standard. A deep learning model was trained on 3629 CT series from 1502 patients (cohort 1) to segment the ureter and extract centerline length. An independent prospective cohort (cohort 2) of 70 patients undergoing radical nephroureterectomy served as the hold-out test set. Each gross specimen was measured twice by one urologist (D1_length and D2_length), with their mean as the reference length (Ref_length). Model-predicted lengths (AI_length) were compared with Ref_length using repeated-measures one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc tests. Determinants of discrepancy were assessed with Spearman correlation and multiple linear regression. Marginal means (± SE) were 266 ± 3.85 mm (D1_length), 273 ± 3.25 mm (D2_length), 269 ± 2.75 mm (AI_length), and 269 ± 3.45 mm (Ref_length). Measurement method had a statistically significant but negligible effect on length (F(3, 207) = 2.73, p = 0.045, η2G = 0.007). D1_length and D2_length differed significantly from Ref_length (both p = 0.002), whereas AI_length was not statistically different from Ref_length (p > 0.999). In regression analysis, reference ureteral length was the only independently associated variable (coefficient - 0.54 mm per mm of reference length, 95% CI - 0.70 to - 0.39; p < 0.001); age, sex, body height, body weight, operation side, and lesion location were not significantly associated. The proposed deep learning pipeline achieved accurate fully automated ureteral segmentation and length measurement across diverse CT acquisition phases and demonstrated close agreement with surgical gross specimen measurements in a prospective clinical cohort, supporting its potential to assist preoperative planning and reduce reliance on manual measurement. The measurement discrepancy was governed primarily by ureteral length itself-with a small systematic underestimation in longer ureters-rather than by patient or procedural factors. However, this tendency, together with the single-center design, and the modest size of the prospective cohort, warrants further multicenter validation before routine clinical deployment.

articles.title: AI-based Hip Fracture Classification from Pelvic X-ray Images Using a Hybrid PEFT-ViT and XGBoost Model.
