articles.abstract: Accurate radiographic classification of hip fractures into femoral neck (intracapsular) versus intertrochanteric (extracapsular) types is essential for surgical planning, yet most AI studies focus on binary detection using large datasets from high-resource regions, with no prior work from the Middle East. This study proposes a Hybrid PEFT-ViT and XGBoost framework for three-class classification of hip radiographs (Normal, Intertrochanteric fracture, Neck of femur fracture), using 768 X-ray images collected from King Abdullah University Hospital (KAUH) in Northern Jordan. A LoRA-fine-tuned ViT-Base/16 backbone extracted fused class-token and patch-token features, which were classified using XGBoost. On an independent test set of 77 radiographs, the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 88.31% (95% CI 79.3-93.7%), a sensitivity of 87.75%, a specificity of 94.28%, and an F1-score of 87.75%, the highest among the evaluated CNN-based (MobileNetV2, DenseNet121) and transformer-based (ViT, DeiT, Swin) baselines. These results show that clinically meaningful hip fracture classification can be achieved using a single-center dataset, providing a practical framework for resource-limited settings, although external validation is still required.

articles.title: Explainability and Clinical Trust of Deep Learning in Glioblastoma Treatment Efficacy Prediction: A Comprehensive Framework.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) treatment response is highly heterogeneous. Predicting outcomes from pre-treatment MRI is a critical unmet need, yet the clinical adoption of "black box" deep learning (DL) models is hindered by a lack of transparency. Robust and holistic validation frameworks still need to be developed to allow clinical trust. A multi-layered eXplainable AI (XAI) pipeline was employed to dissect a previously developed deep learning model trained to predict GBM overall survival. First, the model's visual focus was qualitatively and quantitatively analysed. Second, the model's feature dependence was quantified using input ablation studies. Third, the depth at which class information becomes decodable was traced by linear probing of the internal representations. Finally, the clinical impact of the AI and its explanations was assessed in a multi-reader, multi-case study (37 patients, 4 readers, 3 phases, 444 observations) using Generalised Estimating Equations (GEE) and clustered bootstrapping. Analysis revealed a high-intensity heuristic: hyper-intense pixels at the skull periphery anchored "Long-Term" predictions, while the model defaulted to "Short-Term" based on tumour enhancement in its absence. The ablation study established this dependence, and linear probing pointed in the same direction. In the clinical study, AI assistance significantly improved expert accuracy (OR 1.598, p < 0.01) without artificially boosting confidence (p = 0.561). Importantly, the addition of XAI heatmaps was associated with a change in how experts used the AI score (interaction p < 0.01), and with fewer patients wrongly called long-term survivors. High predictive accuracy can mask reliance on low-level intensity heuristics. While superficial interpretation of saliency maps is perilous, multi-layered audits expose these shortcuts. Clinically, spatial heatmaps were associated with improved expert diagnostic accuracy and a shift in decision-making strategy.

articles.title: Cross-Dataset Reliability of Deep Learning Models for Pressure Injury Staging: a Multiarchitecture Evaluation and Prediction-Error Analysis.
articles.abstract: Deep learning models have been proposed for automated pressure injury staging, but reliability across external wound image datasets remains uncertain. This study assessed cross-dataset reliability across multiple architectures. After dataset curation, including duplicate-image screening, 1081 images from the Pressure Injury Image Dataset (PIID), 1844 images from an institutional Hallym University Medical Center (HUMC) dataset, and 141 Kaggle images were analyzed. Six convolutional neural network and Transformer architectures were trained on PIID or HUMC and evaluated on internal and external datasets without additional fine-tuning or threshold adjustment. The primary outcome was the internal-to-external generalization gap in macro-averaged F1 score. Models trained on PIID achieved a mean internal macro-averaged F1 score of 0.75, decreasing to 0.36 on HUMC and 0.56 on Kaggle. Models trained on HUMC achieved a mean internal macro-averaged F1 score of 0.66, decreasing to 0.53 on both external datasets. No architecture consistently outperformed others in external validation. Prediction-error analysis showed dataset-dependent differences in error direction. Understaging and overstaging errors were defined as predictions below and above the true stage. Models trained on PIID predominantly produced understaging errors on HUMC, and models trained on HUMC predominantly produced overstaging errors on PIID. Exploratory analysis of frozen feature vectors showed limited grouping of images in feature space, with dataset source more closely associated with feature structure than pressure injury stage. These findings support the importance of cross-dataset validation in evaluating automated pressure ulcer staging models. The observed performance degradation and dataset-dependent error patterns suggest sensitivity to dataset-level heterogeneity. Consequently, this study supports two important points. First, in the field of pressure ulcers where image capture protocols are not fixed, external validation using diverse datasets is necessary to evaluate generalization performance. Second, a unified protocol must be included in the data acquisition process to develop reproducible models.

articles.title: Can General-purpose Multimodal AI Reliably Measure Cobb Angles? A Head-to-head Diagnostic Agreement Study of GPT-5.1 and Gemini 3.1 Pro in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
articles.abstract: General-purpose multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) models can interpret radiographs through natural-language prompts, but their quantitative agreement and anatomical traceability in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis remain uncertain. We compared GPT-5.1 and Gemini 3.1 Pro with a joint expert-consensus reference on 125 anonymized standing coronal whole-spine radiographs. Each model evaluated each image once in an independent chat session using the same standardized prompt; only the first response was retained. Outcomes included single-measure absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), mean absolute error (MAE) relative to the reference, Bland-Altman analysis, error-threshold performance, categorical agreement, and end-vertebra concordance. Gemini 3.1 Pro showed higher ICC (0.842 versus 0.587), lower mean bias (3.46° versus 8.68°), lower MAE (5.06° versus 9.62°; paired P < 0.001), and more measurements within 5° of the reference (61.6% versus 24.8%). Agreement with reference categories was 80.0% versus 52.8% for angle-derived severity and 78.4% versus 52.8% for prompt-constrained management categories (both paired P < 0.001). Exact upper end-vertebra agreement was 14.4% versus 8.8%, and exact lower end-vertebra agreement was below 20% for both models. Gemini 3.1 Pro performed better under the tested single-session protocol, but neither model demonstrated sufficient case-level agreement and end-vertebra concordance to support autonomous Cobb-angle measurement. These results are relative to expert consensus and do not establish absolute measurement accuracy or model repeatability. Expert verification remains necessary.

articles.title: Reproducibility and diagnostic performance of ADC for assessing response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multi-ROI comparison analysis from the phase-Ib NABUCCO trial.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: MRI is increasingly used to assess treatment response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), but only qualitatively. This study evaluates the reproducibility and predictive value of quantitative apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), thought to be a non-invasive surrogate for tumor cell density, in patients with MIBC receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: MRI data from 35 patients, enrolled in the Phase-Ib NABUCCO trial, were analyzed. ADC maps were derived from pre- and post-treatment MRI scans. Three independent radiologists assessed multiple regions of interest (ROIs) to evaluate inter-observer agreement and predictive performance for pathological complete response (pCR). ADC values were normalized using muscle tissue as a reference. Additionally, we analyzed the correlation between ADC and cell densities, derived from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) data. RESULTS: ADC measurements from the whole-tumor ROI (n = 25) demonstrated the highest reproducibility (0.98, 95% CI = [0.95-0.99]), but lacked predictive value (AUC = 0.31, 95% CI = [0.12-0.53], p = 0.109). The most hypointense ROI (n = 22) showed the strongest predictive value for pCR (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.57-1], p = 0.025), though with limited reproducibility. The difference between baseline and follow-up ADC values in the hypointense region (n = 20) again showed the highest diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.80, 95% CI = [0.58-0.98], p = 0.015). Although muscle normalization is proposed to reduce scanner variability, it did not improve predictive performance in this cohort and occasionally reduced reproducibility. No significant correlation was found between whole-tumor ADC and cell density. CONCLUSION: Despite analyzing different measurement techniques for ADC values, none was simultaneously reproducible and predictive, nor provided insights into the biology of the tumor. While ADC shows promise in MIBC, there is an urgent need for more standardized, robust imaging biomarkers. KEY POINTS: Question Non-invasive biomarkers are urgently needed to guide bladder-preserving strategies in MIBC. Findings DWI-MRI shows promise, but standardized robust imaging biomarkers are essential for reliable response assessment. Critical relevance statement Standardized or AI-assisted ROI segmentation could improve ADC reproducibility and diagnostic accuracy in multicenter studies.

articles.title: RAPID perfusion CT in acute ischemic stroke: an educational pictorial review of common patterns, pearls, and pitfalls.
articles.abstract: Rapid processing of Perfusion and Diffusion (RAPID) software for CT perfusion (CTP) is a valuable tool for the evaluation of acute ischemic stroke and therapeutic decision-making in extended therapeutic windows. However, automated maps should not be interpreted in isolation. A structured, pattern-based approach, integrating qualitative visual assessment with automated quantitative output and clinical information to refine therapeutic selection, remains essential to mitigate pitfalls and optimize patient care. The aim of this article is to provide an educational pictorial review based on selected illustrative cases of the most common imaging patterns, interpretive pitfalls, and technical features of CTP processed with RAPID software in acute ischemic stroke, that may serve as a practical guide for radiologists and neuroradiologists. KEY POINTS: Question How can radiologists effectively interpret automated RAPID CT perfusion maps in acute ischemic stroke while avoiding common technical traps, diagnostic pitfalls, and anatomical limitations? Findings Integrating qualitative visual assessment, quantitative RAPID outputs, and clinical-vascular data within a structured workflow minimizes diagnostic errors and optimizes patient selection for reperfusion. Critical relevance statement This educational pictorial review provides a practical, pattern-based approach to RAPID CT perfusion interpretation, highlighting clinical applications, technical limitations, software variability, and diagnostic pitfalls to advance everyday neuroradiological practice and personalized stroke management.

articles.title: Endovascular Therapy for Femoropopliteal Artery Lesions Involving the Popliteal Artery: 1-Year Outcomes from a Real-World Multicenter Registry.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate real-world outcomes of endovascular treatment for femoropopliteal lesions involving the popliteal artery and, in a post-hoc exploratory analysis, assess whether anatomical location (P3 vs. P1/P2 segments) was associated with clinical decision-making and prognosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, post-hoc analysis of 946 patients from the prospective PROMISING registry. For this exploratory analysis, patients were stratified according to distal (P3) versus proximal/mid (P1/P2) popliteal artery involvement. Predictors of stent implantation and clinical decision pathways were compared across groups. RESULTS: Overall procedural success was 98.5%, and the 12-month freedom from major adverse events (MAE), defined as a composite of all-cause mortality, major amputation, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization, was 80.1%. Multivariable analysis indicated P3 involvement independently predicted reduced stent implantation (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.46-0.95, p = 0.027). For vessel preparation, the P3 group more frequently utilized plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA, 67.8% vs. 54.8%, p < 0.001) rather than directional atherectomy or specialty balloons. Despite a lower stent implantation rate and greater use of POBA, 12-month freedom from MAE was comparable between the P3 and P1/P2 groups (78.0% vs. 81.2%, p = 0.481). CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis of real-world registry data, popliteal lesion location was associated with differences in operator treatment strategies. P3 involvement was associated with less frequent stent implantation and greater use of plain balloon angioplasty, while 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable between the P3 and P1/P2 groups. These exploratory findings require external validation before they can be used to inform clinical treatment strategies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04826705 (Registered on March 29, 2021).

articles.title: Comparison of Integrated Versus Sequential Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis Systems in Breast Ultrasound: A Prospective Pilot Study on Examination Time, Reproducibility, and Diagnostic Performance.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To compare integrated and sequential artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis (AI-CAD) systems in terms of examination time, reproducibility, and diagnostic performance in breast ultrasound (US). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study included women who underwent breast US at a breast imaging center between February and March 2025. Two real-time AI-CAD systems were evaluated: an integrated system providing simultaneous lesion detection and diagnosis during scanning, and a sequential system in which lesion detection and diagnostic assessment were performed separately. Examination time was assessed in patients who underwent paired breast US examinations with both AI-CAD systems during the same visit, with randomized examination order. Reproducibility was assessed by applying both systems twice to the same breast lesions. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Examination time analysis included 97 patients and showed longer examination time with sequential AI-CAD than with integrated AI-CAD (P < .001), regardless of examination order. Reproducibility analysis included 145 patients with 215 lesions and showed almost perfect agreement between the first and second acquisitions for both systems (integrated vs. sequential: κ = 0.81 vs. 0.83). For the comparison between the first and second acquisitions, κ values for the integrated versus sequential systems were 0.92 versus 0.76 for malignant lesions, 0.79 versus 0.84 for mass lesions, and 1.00 versus 0.75 for nonmass lesions. However, agreement patterns varied across other scan-plane comparisons. Diagnostic performance analysis included 242 patients. Integrated AI-CAD showed higher sensitivity (integrated vs. sequential: 87.6% vs. 76.9%; P < .001), whereas sequential AI-CAD showed higher specificity (integrated vs. sequential: 74.2% vs. 90.0%; P < .001). AUC did not differ between the two systems. CONCLUSION: Integrated and sequential AI-CAD systems showed complementary strengths in breast US. Integrated AI-CAD favored shorter examination time and higher sensitivity, whereas sequential AI-CAD favored higher specificity, with reproducibility differing according to lesion type.

articles.title: Multicenter Comparative Validation of an nnU-Net-Based Automated CT Radiomics Workflow for Acute Pancreatitis Severity Prediction.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Computed tomography radiomics has shown potential for predicting acute pancreatitis (AP) severity, but conventional workflows depend on labor-intensive expert pancreatic segmentation. This study evaluated a no-new-Net (nnU-Net)-based automated segmentation-radiomics workflow against an expert manual-segmentation workflow, using AP severity classification as the downstream task, and assessed the automated workflow externally. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included patients with AP from Center A (n = 214), Center B (n = 56), and Center C (n = 42). Expert manual pancreatic masks served as reference annotations for nnU-Net training and as the comparator for the radiomics workflow. After selecting the optimal nnU-Net configuration, radiomics features were extracted separately from manual and automated regions of interest, and AP severity classifiers were developed using the same analytical framework. Discrimination between the two workflows was compared in the independent internal test cohort using the area under the curve (AUC) and the paired DeLong test, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) and Bonferroni corrections applied to P values. RESULTS: In the internal test cohort, the Light Gradient Boosting Machine classifier achieved AUCs of 0.799 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.683-0.915) and 0.733 (95% CI, 0.593-0.873) with manual and automated segmentations, respectively. The absolute AUC difference was 0.066, and the paired DeLong comparison was not statistically significant after FDR correction (FDR-adjusted p = 0.360; Z = 1.1755, unadjusted p = 0.2398). The automated workflow achieved AUCs of 0.784 (95% CI, 0.653-0.915) in Center B and 0.715 (95% CI, 0.559-0.871) in Center C. The selected 2D nnU-Net achieved a mean Dice coefficient of 0.798 during five-fold cross-validation and 0.726 in the independent internal test cohort. CONCLUSION: The nnU-Net-based automated segmentation-radiomics workflow showed no significant difference in discrimination compared with the expert manual workflow in the internal test cohort. It also maintained moderate discrimination across two external cohorts. These findings support the feasibility of reducing dependence on manual pancreatic segmentation, although the present analysis does not establish formal equivalence or interchangeability.

articles.title: Dual-Lumen Balloon Assisted Onyx Embolization of Middle Meningeal Artery for Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) with liquid embolic agents (LEAs) is increasingly used to manage chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH). Conventional microcatheters require distal wedge positioning of the microcatheter tip or proximal plug formation to prevent reflux and achieve effective distal penetration. Dual-lumen balloon microcatheters limit reflux and enable controlled LEA injection, which may improve procedural efficiency. The evidence base for dual-lumen balloons in CSDH is limited. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive adults with CSDH treated from December 2021 to September 2025. The Scepter XC dual-lumen balloon microcatheter was used to arrest antegrade flow and control Onyx-18 delivery, first distal to the anterior branch origin and then from the MMA trunk into the posterior branch. Outcomes included >50% hematoma thickness reduction and complete resolution on computed tomography (CT), recurrence, retreatment, complications, hospital stay, and procedure time. RESULTS: 152 patients were identified; 33 (21.7%) underwent concomitant surgery and 108 (71.1%) standalone MMAE. Median follow-up was 3 months. This technique achieved >50% hematoma thickness reduction in 90.4% and complete resolution in 70.6% at 3 months or last follow-up. There were no serious adverse events definitely associated with the dual-lumen balloon technique. Overall postprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients (2.6%): transient facial palsy in 2 (1.3%), transient diplopia in 1 (0.7%), and bilateral watershed territory cerebral infarctions without long-term neurological deficits in 1 (0.7%). Median hospital stay was 2 days (IQR 1-4), and median procedure duration was 31.5 minutes (IQR 24.3-48.8). None of the patients who completed follow-up experienced CSDH recurrence or required retreatment. CONCLUSIONS: Scepter XC-assisted Onyx-18 MMAE was technically feasible and associated with high rates of CSDH resorption and resolution, with a safety profile similar to other MMAE techniques and no serious adverse events directly attributable to dual-lumen balloon microcatheter use.

articles.title: Deep learning-based spot weight generation for online adaptive IMPT: implementation and technical feasibility on a clinical delivery system.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the feasibility of a deep learning-based method for generating intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) spot weights to enable a faster, more automated workflow. METHODS: A 3D Attention U-Net with a masked mean absolute error loss generated spot weights from four input channels (optimized plan dose, reference dose, CT image, spot mask), using planned spot weights as labels, and trained and tested on prostate, brain, and lung cases. Robustness was evaluated on target dose metrics only. The workflow was validated in the Eclipse® treatment planning system and delivered on a ProBeam 360° system. RESULTS: For weights in the range 0-5, mean absolute errors were below 0.8 for the prostate and brain models (15.9% and 48.1% of all weights, respectively) and below 1.7 for the lung model (31.2%). Mean relative errors were below 10% for the prostate model (5-65, 83.7%), 20% for the brain model (5-65, 51.7%), and 40% for the lung model (5-110, 68.6%); the remaining weights lay above these ranges and accounted for <0.5% of all weights. Gamma passing rates within the body contours (2%, 2 mm, 10% dose threshold) were 99.73 ± 0.32%, 98.95 ± 0.86%, and 92.75 ± 3.52% for the prostate, brain, and lung models, respectively. All delivered plans met the clinical QA acceptance criteria. CONCLUSION: The proposed framework demonstrates the technical feasibility of generating IMPT spot weights with deep learning and implementing them on a clinical delivery system. Further improvement is needed for heterogeneous sites such as the lung.

articles.title: Initial complete local therapy without systemic therapy versus systemic-therapy-based management in selected patients with oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma: a matched comparative study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare survival outcomes of initial complete metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) without systemic therapy (ST) and ST-based management in patients with oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with oligometastatic RCC (≤5 lesions) treated between 2015 and 2023. Patients were categorized as MDT alone (surgery, radiotherapy, or both, without ST) or ST ± local treatment. One-to-one exact matching between the initial MDT-alone and ST-based groups was performed using six covariates (lesion count, timing of presentation, IMDC risk, Charlson comorbidity index, number of involved organs, and performance status). RESULTS: Among 276 patients (MDT, n = 173; ST, n = 103), 72 pairs were generated after exact matching. Median follow-up was 86.2 months for the MDT and 71.6 months for the ST group in the matched cohort. MDT alone was associated with higher 5-year overall survival (OS) (73.0 % vs. 58.6 %; hazard ratio [HR] 0.45, 95 % confidence interval [CI] 0.26-0.77, p = 0.004) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) (83.7 % vs. 69.8 %; HR 0.35, 95 % CI 0.18-0.67; p = 0.001) in the matched cohort. Progression-free survival (PFS) and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) did not differ between groups. In the MDT alone group, the 5-year cumulative incidence of subsequent ST initiation was 48.6 %. In the whole cohort, the association was consistent across IMDC risk groups (p-interaction = 0.898). CONCLUSIONS: In this selected post-nephrectomy cohort, an initial complete-local-therapy strategy without ST was associated with higher OS and CSS than heterogeneous, predominantly TKI-based ST management, although PFS and DMFS were similar. Given the nonrandomized treatment allocation and residual biological selection, these findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of superiority over contemporary ICI-based therapy.

articles.title: Uncertainty quantification for detecting out-of-distribution cases in deep learning segmentation of head and neck organs of interest.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Quality assurance (QA) of auto-segmentations is necessary for safe clinical deployment. Deep learning models are optimised for data similar to their training set, but reliability drops with out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. This study evaluates whether uncertainty quantification (UQ) can detect OOD inputs arising from distribution shift in head and neck organ of interest (OOI) auto-segmentation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty scores and geometric accuracy of nnU-Net models were evaluated in two experiments. First, as a proof-of-concept, we assessed whether uncertainty scores detect metal artefact (N = 10) from non-artefact cases (N = 10) on a baseline model (mixed training data, N = 620) and a no-metal model (artefact-free training data, N = 620). Second, in a clinically realistic experiment, we split a fine-tuning dataset by uncertainty score to obtain a narrow model (low-uncertainty cases, N = 21) and a broad model (high-uncertainty cases, N = 21). A held-out test set (N = 76) evaluated whether segmentation accuracy differed between uncertainty categories. RESULTS: Both experiments showed that uncertainty scores reflect the learned training distribution. In the supervised experiment, the no-metal model demonstrated greater uncertainty score separation between artefact and non-artefact cases (1.1 × 105 vs 0.6 × 105) than the baseline model (1.1 × 105 vs 0.8 × 105). In the unsupervised experiment, the narrow model performed significantly better on certain than uncertain cases (p = 0.04), while no difference was seen for the broad model (p = 0.34), which did include these cases in training. CONCLUSIONS: Uncertainty quantification can detect distribution shifts in radiotherapy auto-segmentation. This could support automated QA workflows by identifying in-distribution cases and enabling the application of specialised models.

articles.title: Effects of intensive sensorimotor rehabilitation in resting state functional connectivity in a rodent model of Cerebral Palsy.
articles.abstract: Background Sensorimotor stimulation has been shown to protect against brain damage and function impairments following experimental Cerebral Palsy (CP). Functional ultrasound (fUS) gives valuable information about brain connectivity at unprecedented spatial and time resolutions with high translational potential. We tested brain function and connectivity using fUS following experimental CP and the effects of early sensorimotor rehabilitation in the model. Methods Pregnant Wistar rats were exposed to maternal immune challenge at E18-19. Pups received perinatal anoxia at postnatal day 0 (P0) and restriction of the hindlimbs from P2 to P21. Rehabilitation (EETT) used environmental enrichment (EE) and Treadmill Training (TT) from P21 to P28. At P29, fUS was performed to access brain connectivity and graph theoretic analysis was used to distinguish patterns of brain connectivity. Results CP increased intrinsic brain functional connectivity compared to Controls and EETT animals. Connectivity was increased in CP animals in cortical areas related to sensorimotor function and subcortical myelinated structures. EETT animals showed levels of brain connectivity similar to Controls. Conclusions Sensorimotor stimulation changed brain hyperconnectivity profile induced by CP. Brain connectivity pattern alterations can be detected using fUS with high accuracy, suggesting great potential to be used as earlier biomarker for neurodevelopmentalal disorders such as CP.

articles.title: A comparison of continuous-wave fNIRS with quantitative fMRI-derived indices of brain function in the visual cortex.
articles.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) both rely on the phenomenon of neurovascular coupling (NVC) to probe brain activity through their sensitivity to cerebral blood oxygenation. However, the relationship between fNIRS chromophores (oxy- and deoxyhaemoglobin, HbO and HbR), and fMRI (Blood Oxygen Level Dependent and Arterial Spin Labeling, BOLD and ASL) measurements, and whether this relationship remains consistent across subjects and physiological conditions, has only been partially characterised. We acquired concurrent continuous-wave fNIRS and gradient-echo (GE) and spin-echo (SE) BOLD-ASL fMRI in healthy adults (n = 10) during visual stimulation. By applying calibrated fMRI methodology, we examined the relationships between fNIRS-derived haemoglobin modulations and fMRI-derived modulations in macrovascular (GE-) and microvascular (SE-) BOLD signals, cerebral blood flow (CBF), and oxygen metabolism (CMRO₂). Group-level results showed strong temporal cross-modal agreement, with HbO and HbR tightly mirroring all fMRI signal time-courses (|r| > 0.8). A quantitative analysis of trial-by-trial modulations revealed distinct state-dependent behaviours: HbO maintained a stable relationship with the fMRI-derived metrics across conditions, whereas cross-modal relationships between HbR and fMRI-derived metrics substantially strengthened at higher flow-metabolism coupling (FMC), the ratio of CBF to CMRO₂ change, an index of the strength of NVC. Both HbO and HbR were more strongly associated with GE-BOLD than with SE-BOLD. These findings provide a rigorous physiological grounding for fNIRS signal interpretation, demonstrating its utility as a surrogate marker for specific haemodynamic and metabolic parameters.

articles.title: Default mode network mechanisms of trait rumination in treatment-resistant depression and rTMS: evidence from source-localized EEG.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Rumination is a transdiagnostic feature of multiple psychiatric disorders and is a critical risk factor for more severe episodes and poor treatment outcomes in treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) ameliorates both depressive and ruminative symptoms in TRD. While prior literature has linked rumination to abnormal default mode network (DMN) connectivity, the electrophysiological correlates of rumination in the DMN are not well understood. METHODS: Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data were examined in a cohort of 66 TRD subjects who underwent 30 sessions of rTMS treatment for TRD administered to left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). We employed source-localization and calculated four metrics of functional connectivity (Amplitude Envelope Correlation [AEC], weighted Phase Lag Index [wPLI], magnitude-squared coherence, and Spectral Correlation Coefficient [SCC]) across five frequency bands within the DMN to identify the neural correlates of rumination in TRD. Correction for multiple comparisons was performed using the Network Based Statistic (NBS). RESULTS: Baseline severity of rumination and depression were positively correlated, but AEC alpha band connectivity was positively associated only with baseline rumination severity and not depression. Rumination severity prior to treatment was not associated with any other connectivity metric. Severity of rumination and depression decreased following rTMS treatment, but alpha AEC connectivity did not charge after 30 sessions of rTMS treatment. CONCLUSION: Higher DMN connectivity, as measured by alpha-band AEC, is a stable trait-like neurophysiological marker of rumination that is not significantly affected by rTMS administered to left DLPFC.

articles.title: The EFSUMB Guidelines and Recommendations for the Clinical Practice of Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound (CEUS) in Non-Hepatic Applications: Update 2026.
articles.abstract: This is an update on the European Federation of Societies in Ultrasound, Medicine and Biology (EFSUMB) contrast enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) non-hepatic applications guidelines which were last updated in 2017. There has been consolidation of some of the previous applications, particularly, renal and urology, which are now part of routine clinical practice. The most number of publications and areas of research interest have been in the use of CEUS in bowel, endoscopic ultrasound and in neurosonology. A few novel applications have also been tried and show promise, such as in the parathyroids and salivary glands whilst there are a few areas which have previously been researched relatively extensively but have yet to find their clinical utility. Nonetheless, the use of CEUS and its applications have been steadily growing and it is timely that there has been another update on these guidelines which come, as usual, with recommendations on its use from an expert panel.

articles.title: Impact of deep learning image reconstruction on CT radiomics reproducibility in patients with pulmonary nodules.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Ensuring CT feature reproducibility across imaging protocols and reconstruction algorithms is essential for the generalizability of radiomics applications. This study aimed to evaluate the reproducibility of CT radiomic features in pulmonary nodules using deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) compared with conventional reconstruction techniques under different radiation doses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included 94 patients between March and June 2023. Standard- and low-dose CT images were scanned to assess the impact of dose reduction on feature reproducibility. DLIR strengths at low (DLIR-L), medium (DLIR-M), and high (DLIR-H), representing progressive levels of noise suppression, were compared against filtered back projection (FBP) and adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V at 50% strength (ASIR-V-50%) reconstructions. 2264 features were extracted from pulmonary nodules. The concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and the coefficient of variation (CV) were used to evaluate inter-dose reproducibility, inter-reconstruction reproducibility, and feature variability. RESULTS: The mean CCC for inter-dose reproducibility using DLIR-H, ASIR-V-50%, and FBP was 0.934 ± 0.104, 0.922 ± 0.128, and 0.922 ± 0.113, respectively (p = 0.055), with 29.8%, 27.9%, and 20.2% of features showing near-perfect agreement. In low-dose CT, DLIR-L achieved the highest inter-reconstruction reproducibility against ASIR-V-50% (0.950 ± 0.094), with 39.4% of features showing near-perfect agreement. The overall CV across reconstructions was 9.87 ± 20.32%, with 74.0% of features highly stable. Part-solid nodules showed the lowest variability (7.17 ± 13.48%, p < 0.001). Reproducibility improved significantly with increasing nodule size (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: DLIR improves the radiomic feature reproducibility in pulmonary nodules, making it particularly suitable for low-dose CT protocols. However, the robustness tends to decrease with higher DLIR strengths. Nodule characteristics significantly influence variability. KEY POINTS: Question The impact of DLIR on radiomic feature reproducibility across radiation doses and reconstruction methods in pulmonary nodules remains unknown. Findings DLIR-H demonstrated high inter-dose reproducibility, while DLIR-L achieved the highest inter-reconstruction reproducibility; feature variability decreased significantly with increasing nodule size, with 21 robust features identified. Critical relevance statementThis study critically assesses reconstruction-related instability in CT radiomics and identifies DLIR settings and nodule characteristics that influence feature robustness, supporting protocol optimization and more reliable quantitative pulmonary nodule assessment in clinical radiology.

articles.title: Optimizing AI-assisted decision-making in mammography screening: focusing on uncertainties.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate an AI-based decision-support system for mammography interpretation, assessing its impact on diagnostic performance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 130,838 mammograms from 35,709 patients with confirmed follow-up outcomes across multiple centers, using the Digital Database for Screening Mammography (DDSM) for external validation. Representing one of the largest datasets from the Middle East, it evaluates model generalizability in underrepresented populations. An AI super-model incorporated separate UNet-based networks for lesion segmentation, a high-resolution model (4096) for calcifications, a multi-resolution ensemble (4096, 2048, 1024) for macro-scale lesions, and a risk-assessment model for malignancy prediction. Radiologists interpreted images under five scenarios: unaided, AI-assisted, AI as the final decision-maker in uncertain cases, union of radiologist and AI decisions in uncertain cases, and standalone AI. RESULTS: AI assistance significantly enhanced performance across all scenarios. Based on aggregated reader performance, AUC improved from 83.04% (95% CI: 79.8-86.3) unaided to 88.40% (95% CI: 85.6-91.2) in the union scenario (p < 0.001). Sensitivity increased from 54.8% (95% CI: 48.6-61.0) to 83.9% (95% CI: 79.3-88.4) (p < 0.001), and specificity rose from 83.6% (95% CI: 82.0-85.3) to 91.1% (95% CI: 89.8-92.4) (p < 0.001). Multi-resolution segmentation effectively detected calcifications and challenging lesions. DDSM validation confirmed model robustness. AI showed particular promise in aiding less-experienced radiologists in underserved areas to improve early cancer detection. CONCLUSIONS: AI in mammography interpretation improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces uncertainty, supporting early breast cancer detection and optimized screening workflows. KEY POINTS: Question Can an AI-based decision-support system improve the accuracy of mammography interpretation, reduce diagnostic uncertainty, and support less-experienced radiologists? Findings In this retrospective multicenter study, AI-assisted mammography improved sensitivity and specificity, increased cancer detection, and reduced recalls and false positives. Critical relevance statement AI integration in mammography enhances diagnostic accuracy, reduces unnecessary recalls, and supports more confident and efficient clinical decision-making, particularly by improving the performance of less-experienced radiologists in underserved and resource-limited settings where expert interpretation may be limited.

articles.title: MRI for restaging pancreatic cancer.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is a tumor with a dismal prognosis, as the majority of patients are diagnosed when the tumor is not resectable. Neoadjuvant treatment has significantly improved prognosis, but assessing treatment response can be challenging for radiologists. Given the fibrotic nature of the primary tumor, differentiating between residual viable tumor and fibrotic response can be difficult. MRI can have a role in reassessing the primary tumor and disease spread. In this review, we discuss MR techniques that can be used for this assessment, including routinely used sequences (e.g., DWI) and sequences that are not yet routinely included in pancreatic protocols (e.g., T1 mapping, ECV imaging, and USPIO contrast for nodal staging). KEY POINTS: Question Imaging assessment of the response of pancreatic adenocarcinoma to neoadjuvant treatment is difficult and still has limited accuracy. Findings Different MRI sequences and techniques have been suggested as possibly improving this assessment, reflecting on better patient management. Critical relevance statement We summarize the available evidence on MRI for restaging pancreatic carcinoma after neoadjuvant treatment.

articles.title: A case report of pediatric Gardner syndrome and literature review.
articles.abstract: This case report discusses the diagnosis and treatment of a 14-year-8-month-old male patient genetically diagnosed with Gardner syndrome (GS), systematically reviewing the disease's epidemiology, clinical manifestations, imaging advances, and management strategies. The patient presented with a post-influenza A chest wall mass and had prior resections of abdominal/scalp masses. Colonoscopy revealed > 20 adenomatous polyps. Imaging demonstrated multiple craniofacial osteomas and epidermoid cysts. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic APC gene mutation (NM_000038.6:c.4669_4670del (p.Ile1557*) heterozygous variant). GS, a familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) subtype, has an estimated pediatric incidence of 1/8000-1/14,000. Its classic triad comprises colorectal polyps, osteomas, and soft tissue tumors. Recent studies indicate earlier malignant transformation of duodenal polyps in children versus adults, with desmoid tumor incidence reaching 10-20%. In imaging, low-dose CT, panoramic radiography, and contrast-enhanced MRI can improve early detection of bone lesions and soft tissue tumors. Genetic testing (APC/MUTYH) is the pediatric screening gold standard. Optimized chemoprevention (sulindac/celecoxib) and endoscopic monitoring have significantly improved prognoses. This case highlights the urgency of multidisciplinary management and genetic counseling for pediatric GS.

articles.title: Complementary Error Profiles of Human Readers and Large Language Models in Detecting AI-Generated Chest Radiographs: A Comparative Reader Study.
articles.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) and diffusion models can generate realistic chest radiographs, raising concerns for dataset integrity when provenance metadata are absent. We compared authenticity judgments by two radiologists, two nonradiologist physicians, and three frontier LLMs (GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4.8) on 160 posteroanterior radiographs: 40 real NIH ChestX-ray14 images and 120 synthetic images generated from text by three pipelines. Each evaluator judged every image once; the LLM evaluation was repeated twice 3 months later. Balanced accuracy was the primary metric, given 75% synthetic prevalence. The two best evaluators reached nearly identical balanced accuracy from opposite operating points: Gemini 3.5 Flash had the highest point estimate (77.9%; specificity 100%, sensitivity 55.8%) and RAD1 was a close second (75.8%; specificity 55.0%, sensitivity 96.7%), a paired difference of - 2.1 percentage points (95% CI, - 5.8 to 1.2). On repetition, LLM judgments were not fully reproducible and this ordering did not hold. Nonradiologists performed near chance. All four human readers detected diffusion-generated images at 82-100%, whereas the radiologists misclassified 38-45% of real images and the conservative LLMs reached perfect specificity yet detected only 32-72% of LLM-generated images. With laterality markers and borders masked, specificity was 62.5% (Gemini) and 85.0% (GPT-5.5) against 90-100% in same-day unmasked runs. Interevaluator agreement was low throughout (Fleiss' kappa among LLMs 0.213). A frequency-domain baseline reached 98.3% balanced accuracy within this dataset but 12% sensitivity on a held-out generator. Human readers and LLMs failed on different images; visual authenticity assessment alone may be insufficient for provenance verification.

articles.title: Ultrasonography in disaster medicine: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: This narrative review aimed to critically appraise the diagnostic accuracy, clinical impact, and operational feasibility of ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) across the four domains of disaster medicine. A literature search was conducted following the SANRA and PRISMA-trAIce guidelines. Records were identified through an AI-assisted literature-discovery tool (the Undermind Deep-Search platform, interrogating the Semantic Scholar corpus) run on 15 June 2025, rather than through an independent structured multi-database search. Candidate references were screened manually against pre-specified eligibility criteria by a single reviewer, with the search parameters independently verified by the senior author. Of 71 records identified, 63 met the inclusion criteria. The included studies comprised 32 original studies, 10 systematic or scoping reviews, 20 narrative or operational papers, and one guideline. In CBRN scenarios, lung ultrasound demonstrated sensitivities of 90-97% for COVID-19 pneumonia versus 60-69% for chest radiography while minimizing healthcare worker exposure. For blast and ballistic injuries, FAST showed a pooled sensitivity of 92.1% (95% CI: 87.8-95.6) and specificity of 98.7% (95% CI: 96.0-99.9) for intra-abdominal hemorrhage. In natural disasters, ultrasound altered management in up to 44% of patients. Post-disaster applications included vascular access, tube confirmation, and complication monitoring. Ultraportable POCUS demonstrates diagnostic utility and operational feasibility across multiple disaster domains. However, evidence quality varies significantly, and standardized protocols remain lacking. Prospective studies linking ultrasound deployment to improved patient outcomes are needed. KEY POINTS: Question When disasters disable conventional imaging, how does ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography perform for diagnosis, triage, and procedural guidance across the four domains of disaster medicine? Findings Across 63 studies, FAST reached 92.1% pooled sensitivity for hemoperitoneum, lung ultrasound 90-97% versus 60-69% for radiography; management changed in up to 44%. Critical relevance statement This review critically appraises ultraportable ultrasound across all four disaster domains, showing that radiation-free bedside imaging accelerates triage, conserves scarce CT capacity, and extends radiological expertise through tele-guidance, while exposing an evidence base still lacking prospective outcome data.

articles.title: Limited incremental value and cross-cohort transferability of CT radiomics for survival prediction after TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether pretreatment CT radiomics adds information for overall survival (OS) prediction among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and assess frozen imaging-model performance in an independent cohort. METHODS: This retrospective study included 221 WAW-TACE and 98 HCC-TACE-SEG patients with pretreatment arterial and portal venous CT. Incremental value of a tumor-radiomics Random Survival Forest score (R1) beyond cohort-specific clinical Cox models (C0) was evaluated within each cohort using 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. External validation was restricted to frozen WAW-trained R1 models (Top-K = 5, 10, 15) applied to HCC-TACE-SEG without refitting; the combined C0 + R1 model was not externally validated. RESULTS: WAW-TACE included 162 deaths and HCC-TACE-SEG 86 deaths. In WAW-TACE, C0, R1 Top-K = 15, and C0 + R1 achieved C-indices of 0.646 ± 0.043, 0.593 ± 0.049, and 0.639 ± 0.045, respectively. Corresponding HCC-TACE-SEG estimates were 0.496 ± 0.087, 0.530 ± 0.072, and 0.495 ± 0.094. Thus, R1 did not consistently improve cohort-specific clinical reference models. In frozen external application, Top-K = 5, 10, and 15 achieved C-indices of 0.463 (95% CI 0.397-0.532), 0.535 (0.468-0.608), and 0.528 (0.460-0.598), respectively. CONCLUSION: The evaluated models showed no consistent incremental value for OS prediction within these TACE cohorts and limited frozen-model discrimination in the clinically distinct HCC-TACE-SEG cohort. These findings do not support clinical use of these models or establish a general limitation of CT radiomics.

articles.title: Machine learning-assisted monitoring of radiofrequency ablation in hepatic tumors using spectral traces.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate intraoperative assessment of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) margins in hepatic malignancies remains a significant clinical challenge. METHODS: This study investigates the efficacy of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for objective, spatially resolved discrimination of ablated tissue, viable tumor, and normal parenchyma in 10 ex vivo liver specimens. Analysis of visible-near-infrared (VNIR) reflectance revealed distinct spectral signatures, characterized by a consistent monotonic hierarchy (ablated < normal < tumor), enabling reliable tissue differentiation. Segmentation performance was systematically evaluated using four supervised classifiers: Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). The total delineated tissue area exhibited notable inter-method variability, ranging from 137,283 to 189,289 pixels (+ 37.9%), underscoring sensitivity to classifier architecture. RESULTS: Nevertheless, all approaches maintained biologically coherent tissue distributions, with normal parenchyma predominating (44-56%), followed by tumor (25-39%) and ablated regions (17-20%). That is consistently indicating the necessity for monitoring ablative margins. SAM, SVM, and LDA classifiers achieved class-specific detection errors around 3.5% and 18%. LDA attained the highest overall accuracy (94.5%), demonstrating the potential of HSI for reliable, intraoperative image-guided tissue characterization. Dimensionality reduction across 462 spectral bands identified an optimal discriminative window within 643-698 nm, supporting the development of streamlined multispectral systems. CONCLUSION: Overall, HSI is neither a contact nor destructive modality for quantitative RFA assessment. Despite classifier-dependent variability necessitating standardized or ensemble strategies, these findings support its prospective integration into real-time surgical guidance, pending in vivo validation.

articles.title: Predicting advanced-stage recurrence in resected hepatocellular carcinoma using preoperative gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI radiomics.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a preoperative gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI-based radiomics model for predicting the time to advanced-stage recurrence in patients undergoing resection for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage 0/A HCC who underwent resection between 2009 and 2014. Patients were temporally divided into training (n = 272; 2009-2011) and validation (n = 210; 2012-2014) cohorts. Time to advanced-stage recurrence was defined as the interval from resection to macrovascular invasion and/or extrahepatic metastasis. Two radiologists segmented tumors on hepatobiliary phase images, followed by 3-mm peritumoral expansion and propagation to co-registered dynamic T1- and T2-weighted images. After extraction of Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative-compliant features, a radiomics model was developed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression. Model performance and inter-reader reproducibility of binary risk stratification were evaluated using the concordance index (C-index) and Cohen's kappa, respectively. RESULTS: Five-year advanced-stage recurrence occurred in 15% of the training (42/272) and validation (32/210) cohorts. In the validation cohort, the radiomics model yielded a C-index of 0.716 (95% CI, 0.631-0.801). This outperformed the preoperative BCLC (0.597; 95% CI 0.551-0.644) and Hong Kong Liver Cancer (0.594; 95% CI 0.516-0.672) staging systems, and was equivalent to the postoperative clinicopathological model (0.716; 95% CI 0.626-0.807). Radiomic-based risk stratification showed good inter-reader reproducibility (kappa = 0.757). CONCLUSION: The preoperative radiomics model outperformed staging systems and was comparable to the postoperative clinicopathological model in predicting advanced-stage recurrence, relying entirely on noninvasive data.

articles.title: Sinonasal Ewing sarcoma with hard-palate erosion.
Establishing the reliability of non-contrast 4D flow in congenital heart disease at 1.5T.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: 4D flow has been shown to correlate well with 2D phase-contrast (2D PC) flow measurements, although most of the current literature is based on post-contrast imaging. OBJECTIVE: Given recent interest in non-contrast techniques, we hypothesized that non-contrast 4D flow (NC 4D Flow) would correlate well with 2D PC and ventricular stroke volumes. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A prospective cohort of pediatric and young adult patients with suspected/confirmed congenital heart disease (CHD) underwent cardiac MRI at 1.5T with acquisition of NC 4D Flow and 2D PC. Pearson correlation, linear mixed-effect correlations, and Bland-Altman comparisons were performed to compare these methods with secondary analyses of internal consistency and image quality/noise. RESULTS: In our cohort of 30 patients (age, 8-20 years), NC 4D Flow correlated strongly with 2D PC for net flow (r=0.76), peak velocity (r=0.9, P<0.001), and regurgitant fraction (r=0.75, P<0.001). By Bland-Altman comparison, NC 4D Flow was 10.1% lower for net flows and 18.9% higher for peak velocity compared to 2D PC. NC 4D Flow also slightly underestimated ventricular stroke volumes (18.1% lower for ascending aorta vs. left ventricular stroke volume and 13.9% lower for main pulmonary artery vs. right ventricular stroke volume). Both datasets were internally consistent; 2D PC had a higher relative signal intensity, but no difference in signal-to-noise or contrast-to-noise ratios (SNR/CNR). CONCLUSION: Non-contrast 4D flow correlates well with 2D PC in CHD with a slight underestimation in flows and overestimation in peak velocities, but good internal consistency and comparable SNR/CNR.

articles.title: MRI-Based 2.5D Multi-Instance Deep Learning for Differentiating Pathological Subtypes of Brain Metastases From Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Distinct treatment strategies for small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases require accurate noninvasive subtyping. PURPOSE: To develop and externally validate a biparametric MRI-based 2.5D multi-instance learning (MIL) deep learning (DL) model for discriminating SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases, with performance compared against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models. STUDY TYPE: Retrospective. POPULATION: This study included 366 patients from four institutions. Center 1 provided the training set (n = 199; mean age, 63.88 ± 10.79 years; 72.36% male) and an internal tuning set (n = 85; mean age, 64.73 ± 9.53 years; 67.06% male). Centers 2-4 were pooled into a single external test set (n = 82; mean age, 62.26 ± 10.60 years; 63.41% male). FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 1.5 T and 3.0 T; contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery imaging. ASSESSMENT: The 2.5D-MIL model was benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models and evaluated on internal tuning and pooled external test sets. STATISTICAL TESTS: Shapiro-Wilk, Student's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and DeLong tests were used. Performance measures included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals and classification and calibration metrics. Statistical significance was defined as two-sided p < 0.05. RESULTS: In the internal tuning set, AUCs were 0.842 (2.5D-MIL), 0.740 (clinical), 0.710 (radiomics), and 0.747 (3D-DL). In the external test set, AUCs were 0.826 (2.5D-MIL), 0.826 (clinical), 0.696 (radiomics), and 0.664 (3D-DL). Differences between 2.5D-MIL and the clinical (p = 1.000), radiomics (p = 0.139), and 3D-DL (p = 0.119) models were not significant. DATA CONCLUSION: The MRI-based 2.5D-MIL model showed potential for noninvasive differentiation of SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases. Larger prospective studies are needed before clinical use. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

articles.title: Evaluating Perfusion Quantification for Phase-Resolved Functional Lung MRI Using Gaussian Filtering.
articles.abstract: Phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI enables contrast-free lung perfusion quantification (QQuant). Current quantification uses a single median value per slice of maximal blood exchange fraction (ΔS), which limits regional assessment, whereas regional ΔS causes artifacts. This retrospective study aims to optimize QQuant by applying Gaussian filtering to ΔS to improve intrascan/interscan repeatability in healthy volunteers, while evaluating whether the optimized QQuant retains agreement with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) patients and exhibits a physiologically plausible gravity-dependent perfusion gradient. Analysis was performed on 29 healthy subjects (11 female, age: 19-33 years), 20 COPD patients (three female, age: 46-76 years) and 15 CTEPH patients (six female, age: 44-82 years), scanned at 1.5 T. Healthy subjects underwent four PREFUL scans in two sessions. Patients just underwent one PREFUL and DCE scan. QQuant maps were calculated while applying different Gaussian filter options to ΔS. In patients, PREFUL-derived QQuant maps were coregistered to DCE-derived pulmonary blood flow (PBF) maps for global and voxel-wise correlations. In healthy subjects, the gravity-dependent perfusion gradient was quantified by linear regression of slice-wise QQuant across five coronal slices. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved intrascan and interscan repeatability in healthy subjects (mean bias: ≤ 2.94 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.2) compared with the current slice median setting (mean bias: ≥ 3.75 mL/100 mL; Cohen's d: 0.68). Correlations with PBF remained stable after filtering (σ = 1.5) in COPD (filtered vs. default ΔS: global r = 0.57 vs. r = 0.59, voxel-wise r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.32) and CTEPH (global r = 0.32 vs. r = 0.28, voxel-wise r = 0.40 vs. r = 0.41), all significant except global CTEPH. The filtered QQuant maps showed a significant gravity-dependent perfusion gradient (ΔS filtered σ = 1.5) of 1.47 mL/min/100 mL/cm. Gaussian filtering ΔS with σ = 1.5 improved QQuant repeatability while preserving DCE-MRI agreement and is therefore recommended. The observed gravity-dependent perfusion gradient confirms physiological plausibility, supporting potential in clinical use.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Inguinal Node Relapse Risk in Anal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Following Chemoradiotherapy Omitting Prophylactic Inguinal Node Irradiation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Prophylactic inguinal node irradiation (PINI) is standard in chemoradiotherapy for anal squamous cell carcinoma. However, PINI increases toxicity, including bowel and sexual dysfunction, bone marrow suppression, and lymphoedema. Evidence on inguinal node relapse risk without PINI remains limited, warranting systematic review. METHODS: A systematic literature review was performed in accordance with the PRISMA standards using using Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library and Pubmed for relevant studies between 1980 and 2025. Studies of > 10 patients treated with chemoradiotherapy without PINI and a minimum FU of 24 months were included. Data on stage, recurrence, staging investigations, and radiotherapy technique was extracted and analysed. RESULTS: Nine papers were identified satisfying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, included 727 patients. All 9 reported individual outcomes for stages grouped as T1/2 and T3/4, 6 papers detailed outcomes for individual stages. The pooled estimated risk of lymph node relapse in T1/2 patients is 8.0% (95% CI 6.0-10.6). The pooled analysis for T1 and T2 tumours respectively were 2.20% (95% CI 0.5-8.3) and 8.7 (95% CI 5.4-13.7). CONCLUSIONS: The quantification of inguinal relapse rates supports existing clinical practise that in selected patients, with T1 tumours or the frail and co-morbid population, it may be appropriate to omit PINI. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Following the recently published ACT4 study, suggesting that reduction of dose does not reduce morbidity, this research suggests that exclusion of inguinal nodes in early-stage tumours may be an alternative strategy and should be investigated further in clinical trials.

articles.title: Prandial Effects on Intravoxel Incoherent Motion Quantification in the Liver.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility of detecting prandial (i.e., meal) induced changes in microvascular flow in the liver, including changes in the spatial distribution of flow velocities, using intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) MRI. METHODS: Thirteen (n = 13) healthy volunteers underwent two liver MR exams: one preprandial after fasting and one postprandial after ingesting nutrition shakes. IVIM data were acquired four times: twice preprandial to evaluate repeatability using coefficients of variation (CV) and twice postprandial to evaluate meal-induced changes relative to preprandial estimates. 4D flow MRI was acquired once pre- and postprandial to estimate portal venous flow rate, which was normalized by liver volume to evaluate correlations with IVIM. IVIM estimates of the diffusion coefficient (D), R2-corrected perfusion signal fraction (Fc), blood velocity standard deviation (Vb), and spatial volumes associated with slow microvascular flow (Ω1), fast microvascular flow (Ω2), and major vessels (Ω3) were determined. RESULTS: Significantly (p ≤ 0.01) higher Vb and Ω2 volume and lower Ω1 volume were observed postprandial compared to preprandial. The magnitudes of the postprandial changes in Vb, Ω1 volume, and Ω2 volume (|median relative change| ≥ 10.2%, 48.4%, and 13.7%, respectively) were greater than the corresponding repeatability (CV = 5.19%, 21.3%, and 8.13%, respectively). Significant (p = 0.01) correlation between liver volume-normalized portal venous flow rate and Vb was observed. CONCLUSION: The potential of IVIM to detect physiological (e.g., prandial-induced) changes in microvascular flow in the liver was demonstrated. IVIM data may need to be acquired in a fasting state to avoid confounding prandial effects on IVIM-derived microvascular flow estimates.

articles.title: Learning from the unseen: synthetic data for scoliosis AI segmentation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce. METHODS: We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset. RESULTS: On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable. CONCLUSION: Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Acute glenoid rim fractures: reliability of linear and surface area methods for CT-based bone loss assessment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We wanted to investigate and compare the reliability of two measuring methods for glenoid bone loss, one linear- and one surface area method, in acute glenoid fractures after dislocation. This was an experimental study. METHOD: Thirty CT-shoulder scans in patients with an acute glenoid rim fracture were measured in a lateral"en face" view in 2D and 3D by two independent assessors. In 10 of 30 patients contralateral shoulder CT-scan was obtained for reference circle placement. Intra- and interrater reliability was analysed by Intra Class Correlation. Wilcoxon signed rank test was performed for comparison of bone loss estimates between methods. RESULTS: The reliability ranged from 0.85 to 0.97 for the two methods in both 2D and 3D, which is considered good to excellent. The bone loss estimates were significantly larger with linear method than area method. Drawing of a best-fitting-circle had a good reliability between assessors. CONCLUSIONS: Linear- and surface area methods demonstrated comparable reliability in assessing glenoid bone loss in acute fractures and we found no difference between 2D- and 3D-modalities. However, linear methods may overestimate defect in cases with irregular fracture lines, suggesting area method may be preferable in acute fractures.

articles.title: Implementation of a Structured Peer Learning Program and Missed Critical Findings in a Large Integrated Radiology Practice: A Baseline Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The American College of Radiology (ACR) defines peer learning as nonpunitive, education-centered case review, separated from individual performance evaluation. We describe a program designed against ACR criteria in a large integrated practice and report first-cycle metrics, including missed critical findings-a narrow subset of major misses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective analysis spanned 283 radiologists across more than 100 sites between March 30 and May 14, 2026. Cases entered through voluntary worklist submission, risk-event referral, and departmental escalation, and were adjudicated by a fellowship-trained coordinator. A missed critical finding (MCF) required both a finding on the institutional critical results list (provider notification within 30 minutes) and a 4B classification, with agreement between two independent reviewers. Exact (Poisson) 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. RESULTS: Of 702 submissions, 489 (69.7%) were Learning Opportunities, 187 (26.6%) Great Calls, and 26 (3.7%) Agrees. Of 283 radiologists, 182 (64.3%) submitted at least one case, and 213 (75.3%) received feedback; two conferences were held. Of 17 candidates, reviewers concurred on 7 at initial review; the 10 discordant were resolved by consensus, none meeting criteria. Across 409,122 interpreted studies, the confirmed MCF rate was 0.017 per 1000 (95% CI 0.007-0.035). Seven radiologists (2.5%) had one event; none had more. No confirmed event had been independently filed as a safety event. CONCLUSION: The MCF rate reflects a narrow, time-critical subset ascertained with unmeasured sensitivity against a diluted denominator. It is a conservative internal baseline, not a measure of diagnostic accuracy or individual performance.

articles.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of a quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-structured reporting pipeline that integrates quantitative MRI software with large language models (LLMs) for structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers and generating clinician-facing report conclusions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 192 patients with 3D T1 and 2D or 3D FLAIR MRI images from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative database were randomly selected. A deep-learning model generated structured report findings based on nine indices related to brain atrophy, white matter hyperintensities, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) space abnormalities, and compared with neuroradiologist-generated reference reports. Four LLMs (GPT-OSS 20B, MedGemma 4B, Phi-3, and Llama 3.1 8B) generated clinician-facing conclusions from the structured findings. Generated conclusions were evaluated using a five-point Likert scale across four metrics (accuracy, relevance, clarity, and satisfaction). Output errors were assessed across four categories: language, omission, addition, and numeric errors. RESULTS: Structured report findings demonstrated high accuracy for CSF space analysis (77.6%-97.9%). Performance for ordinal visual scales was lower under strict matching (27.1%-57.8%) but improved with a one-grade tolerance (91.7%-97.4%). Among LLMs, GPT achieved the highest scores across most metrics (median score 5) and exhibited the lowest output error rates. Smaller models (Phi-3 and Llama 3.1 8B) showed overall lower performance, with more language, omission, and addition errors. MedGemma demonstrated intermediate performance, but the highest rate of numeric errors. CONCLUSION: Our quantitative MRI-to-structured reporting pipeline, integrating quantitative MRI software with LLM-based conclusion generation, might be feasible for automated structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers.

articles.title: Added Value of CT Bone Reading Software in the Detection of Subtle Bone Metastases From Breast Cancer: Comparison with Standard Thorax CT.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to evaluate the additional diagnostic value of CT Bone Reading software in detecting rib metastases on thoracic computed tomography in patients with breast cancer and to examine its effectiveness on lesion detection, evaluation time, and inter-reader agreement. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 110 patients with breast cancer and bone metastases who underwent both thoracic computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography-CT scans between January 2022 and January 2026. For lesion-level assessment, suspected rib lesions were also evaluated using available longitudinal follow-up imaging. Two radiologists independently evaluated conventional CT and CT Bone Reading images in separate reading sessions at least 2 weeks apart. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen's κ statistic. RESULTS: In lesion-based analysis with conventional CT, Reader 1 detected 510 lesions (81.6%) and Reader 2 detected 577 lesions (92.3%), while CT Bone Reading allowed for the detection of an additional 115 (22.5%) and 48 (8.3%) lesions for Readers 1 and 2, respectively. The additionally detected lesions demonstrated a non-uniform distribution, with a marked predominance in the mid-rib region (levels 5th-8th). CT Bone Reading-assisted evaluation enabled the detection of significantly smaller lesions compared to routine CT for both readers (Reader 1: 8.0 mm vs 5.0 mm; Reader 2: 7.0 mm vs 5.0 mm; P < 0.001 for both). Evaluation time was significantly decreased from 129.22 ± 27.22 s to 64.94 ± 17.16 s for Reader 1 and from 122.99 ± 26.04 s to 64.44 ± 18.71 s for Reader 2 (P < 0.001 for both). Inter-reader agreement was excellent for measurements obtained by CT Bone Reading-derived evaluation (ICC ≥0.965; κ ≥0.947). CONCLUSION: CT Bone Reading software increases the detection rates of rib lesions, reduces interpretation times, and demonstrates excellent inter-reader reproducibility compared to conventional CT assessment, with less experienced readers achieving the highest incremental throughput. By providing a comprehensive and continuous view of the ribs, this technique has the potential to improve diagnostic performance without additional radiation exposure, particularly in anatomically complex regions such as the mid ribs. Ultimately, this approach can enhance workflow efficiency during routine clinical practices.

articles.title: Radhawk: An AI-driven Recommender for Pediatric Radiology Education.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: The unprecedented growth of technology and unfiltered information has led to cognitive overload and educational gaps in radiology. Radiologists and trainees often require "just-in-time" educational content while interpreting unfamiliar or infrequently encountered examinations, yet identifying reliable and appropriately targeted resources within the time constraints of the reading room can be challenging. This need is particularly relevant in pediatric radiology, where normal imaging appearances vary with age and development. Radhawk was developed as a scalable, artificial intelligence-driven intelligent tutoring system that delivers personalized, real-time educational resources to learners and radiologists, creating a precision curriculum tailored to each user's needs and clinical context. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Radhawk integrates with existing picture archiving and communication systems and a custom learning management system (RADiology's Intelligent Adaptive Learning). It utilizes natural language processing and machine learning algorithms to analyze imaging study information and provides results based on user preferences. The system's scalable architecture is built on Amazon Web Services, ensuring adaptability across multiple hospital systems. RESULTS: Radhawk successfully provides tailored recommendations for educational materials, including interactive courses, anatomical references, and case studies. Key features include: (1) Generation of personalized curricula based on learner performance and needs, (2) Presentation of age and gender-matched "normal" images for comparison, (3) Creation of user-specific heat maps to identify strengths and areas for improvement, and (4) Incorporation of expert subspecialist preferences to inform user choices. CONCLUSION: Radhawk replaces generic web searches with a knowledge-focused approach, providing instant access to high-quality, relevant resources. This precision education solution has the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy, enhance learning experiences, and address the shortage of specialized pediatric radiologists. Future plans include external testing across multiple pediatric radiology departments to validate Radhawk's scalability, acceptance, and value in real-world settings.

articles.title: Short-Duration [18F]florbetapir PET Reconstructions: Centiloid Agreement and Temporal-Window Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Shorter [18F]florbetapir PET acquisitions could improve workflow, but the effects of reconstruction duration and temporal-window position on Centiloid values are not well characterized. We evaluated quantitative agreement across short-duration reconstructions, temporal-window effects, and visual agreement. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included a primary cohort of 32 patients with early 1-, 2-, and 5-min reconstructions and a 10-min reference. A temporal-window cohort of 22 patients underwent early and late 5-min analysis. A validation cohort of 37 examinations underwent early, centered, and late 1- and 5-min reconstructions and a 10-min reference. Two readers independently classified early 1-min, early 5-min, and 10-min images across three separate reading sessions. Centiloid agreement was assessed using paired differences, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, and categorical agreement. RESULTS: In the primary cohort, mean differences from the 10-min reference were -3.70, -2.97, and -1.65 CL for early 1-, 2-, and 5-min reconstructions, respectively. In the temporal-window cohort, late 5-min values averaged 2.86 CL higher than early values. The validation cohort reproduced both findings: early-to-late shifts were +5.53 CL at 1 min and +3.07 CL at 5 min. In the reader study, agreement with 10 min was 70.3%-86.5% at 1 min and 94.6%-100% at 5 min; interreader κ was 0.49, 0.77, and 0.89 at 1, 5, and 10 min, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Early short-duration reconstructions yielded systematically lower Centiloid values, while later temporal windows yielded higher values at fixed duration. Visual agreement with 10 min was high at 5 min but lower at 1 min. Reconstruction duration and frame timing should be standardized before abbreviated protocols are considered substitutes for standard 10-min imaging.

articles.title: Moyamoya-Type Collaterals in ACTA2 p. Arg179 Related Arteriopathy: Challenging the Paradigm of Absent Neovascularization-A Longitudinal DSA Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: ACTA2 p. Arg179 variants can cause a distinctive cerebrovascular arteriopathy historically described lacking classic moyamoya basal collaterals. Limited data on collateral architecture and surgical outcomes have led to uncertainty regarding revascularization strategies. The purpose of this study is to provide a systematic longitudinal DSA assessment of collateral patterns and postoperative findings in pediatric ACTA2-associated cerebrovascular disease. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Ten pediatric patients with genetically confirmed ACTA2 mutations underwent DSA imaging. Eight consecutive patients with neurological instability and confirmed hemodynamic compromise underwent surgical revascularization (indirect or combined direct-indirect). Two patients with stable neurological status were managed conservatively. Paired DSA (7 patients) and magnetic resonance angiography (5 patients) were performed at baseline and follow-up of the operated cohort. Collaterals were classified as classic moyamoya-type, distal moyamoya-type, leptomeningeal, or duropial. Postoperative revascularization was graded using Matsushima classification. RESULTS: Mean baseline vessel calibers demonstrated marked proximal ectasia (petrous ICA 8.4 ± 2.8 mm vs. normative 3.8 ± 0.4) transitioning to distal stenosis (supraclinoid ICA 2.6 ± 0.7 mm vs. normative 3.3 ± 0.3). Classic moyamoya-type collaterals were present in 2 patients at baseline and in 5 patients at follow-up. Postoperative Matsushima grading demonstrated Grade A/B in 6 patients, with surgical collateralization remaining patent and sufficient up to 14 years. CONCLUSIONS: ACTA2 p. Arg179 related cerebral arteriopathy demonstrates moyamoya-type collaterals challenging the historical paradigm of absent collateralization. Robust surgical neovascularization comparable to idiopathic moyamoya may support revascularization in symptomatic pediatric patients with confirmed hemodynamic compromise.

articles.title: 2024-2025 Academic Neuroradiology Workforce and Practice Survey: Faculty FTE and Effort, Recruitment and Retirement Benchmarks.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Rising RVU targets and clinical workloads in academic neuroradiology raise concerns about diagnostic accuracy, patient safety, faculty burnout, and erosion of education/research missions.
