This national survey of division chiefs characterized current practice patterns, effort models, moonlighting, operational factors, compensation, protected time, grant support, and perceptions of sustainable productivity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Web-based survey of academic neuroradiology division chiefs (American Society of Neuroradiology directory), with up to three reminders. 51 responses were collected anonymously and analyzed descriptively in Microsoft Excel. Questions covered workforce, clinical effort models, workload exceedance drivers, moonlighting, leadership protected time, and grant support. RESULTS: Divisions had median 11 FTE (25th-75th: 7-17.25); faculty were mostly full-time (median 90% at 1.0 FTE). Retirement risk was low short-term (median 0% in 2 years, 10% in 5 years); median 2 hires/year. Median clinical effort was 74% cFTE. Effort models split between shift-based (47%) and RVU-target (45%; typically, 40th-70th percentile AAARAD); volume caps used in only 8%. Targets were frequently exceeded, mainly due to moonlighting/financial incentives (49%) and voluntary work (32%). Moonlighting was offered in 52% of divisions (median 50% participation), yielding typical additional income of $26K-$100K/year. Protected effort medians: 20% (division chiefs), 10% (fellowship directors). Grant support was commensurate with funding in most divisions; 62% received "cap gap" support for federal grants. CONCLUSION: Academic neuroradiology faces intense clinical demands, and relies heavily on voluntary and incentivized faculty moonlighting. These findings highlight the need for accurate productivity benchmarks, operational improvements, and stronger institutional protections to sustain quality, safety, faculty satisfaction, and the academic mission.
authors: ASNR Neuroradiology Division Chief Working Group

articles.title: Advanced Practice Providers in Spinal CSF Leak Programs: A Multi-Institutional Study of Current Roles and Perceived Impact on Patient Care.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Advanced practice providers (APPs), including nurse practitioners and physician assistants, are increasingly integrated into radiology practices. However, their utilization and clinical responsibilities in dedicated spinal CSF leak programs have not been characterized. Using a multicenter survey, we investigated APP training, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges of APP integration at US spinal CSF leak programs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A survey was distributed to physicians at US institutions with dedicated spinal CSF leak programs and APP involvement. Candidate institutions were identified through the International Society for Spinal CSF Leak and American Society of Spine Radiology. Survey questions addressed program characteristics, APP training and structure, clinical responsibilities, perceived impact, and challenges. Responses were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Twelve institutions completed the survey. Eight (67%) reported caring for more than 250 spinal CSF leak patients annually. APPs included nurse practitioners at 4 centers (33%), physician assistants at 3 (25%), and both at 5 (42%); 7 centers (58%) had APPs dedicated exclusively to spinal CSF leak care. APP training was primarily informal and on-the-job at all institutions. Common primary APP responsibilities included obtaining outside imaging, patient intake and symptom review, procedure and sedation orders, informed consent, post-procedural follow-up, pain management, and treatment of rebound intracranial hypertension. Shared APP and physician responsibilities commonly included outside record review, determining evaluation urgency, preliminary imaging review, sedation assessment, and multidisciplinary coordination. Procedural responsibilities such as lumbar puncture, intrathecal contrast administration, myelography planning, and CSF leak treatment were primarily performed by physicians in most programs. At least 75% of respondents strongly agreed that APP participation improved continuity of care, patient communication/accessibility, clinic efficiency, patient satisfaction, physician administrative burden, and multidisciplinary coordination. Common barriers included funding/support, billing/reimbursement, and limited procedural privileges. CONCLUSIONS: APPs are widely integrated into dedicated spinal CSF leak programs, with substantial involvement in pre-procedural evaluation, care coordination, and post-procedural management, while advanced myelography and CSF leak treatment remain predominantly physician-directed. APP participation was perceived to improve patient care and clinical workflow. These findings provide a framework for APP integration into specialized spinal CSF leak programs.

articles.title: Automated Detection of Endoleaks in CT Angiography Using a Single Deep Learning Model.
articles.abstract: AIM: Detecting endoleaks on post-EVAR CT scans, especially in the presence of artifacts caused by embolic agents like Onyx, is a challenging but critical task. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based method for endoleak detection using a single object detection model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective dataset comprising 249 CT scans was used, divided into training (129 scans) and test (120 scans) datasets. Ground truth annotations were obtained through 3D manual segmentation, and a preprocessing pipeline was applied. The model was trained on slices extracted from the training dataset and validated using standard metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, and AUC. RESULTS: The model achieved high performance at both the per-slice and per-series levels. Per-slice detection yielded a ROC AUC of 96%, with a sensitivity of 91%, specificity of 93%, PPV of 55%, and NPV of 99%. At the per-series level, sensitivity and specificity were 93% and 95%, respectively. Notably, our method introduces a per-slice detection metric, which was not reported in previous studies, and uses a single model, making it computationally efficient and easy to train. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for endoleak detection, offering a robust and efficient tool for clinical practice. Future work could focus on expanding the dataset and integrating additional predictive capabilities, such as endoleak classification and localization.

articles.title: Percutaneous Deep Venous Arterialization Using the Boomerang® Catheter System.
Ex Vivo Histopathological Validation of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging for Diagnosing Intimal and Medial Calcification in a Single Femoropopliteal Lesion.
articles.abstract: Optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) is available to guide atherectomy for severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions in patients with lower extremity artery disease, although its diagnostic accuracy has not been histologically validated. We evaluated the diagnostic capability of OFDI through histopathological co-registration. A total of 38 OFDI cross-sectional images from a single vessel in one patient were successfully co-registered with corresponding histological sections and analyzed. The internal elastic lamina was not identified in 52.6% of images. OFDI detected 60.2% of all calcifications identified histologically, with substantially higher detection rates for intimal than medial calcification (72.3% vs 30.8%). These findings indicate that OFDI provides acceptable assessment of intimal calcification but has limited capability for visualizing the medial layer in severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Recognition of these limitations may facilitate more appropriate pre-procedural planning for atherectomy in patients with severely calcified femoropopliteal disease.

articles.title: Balloon-occluded pulmonary arteriography and n-butyl cyanoacrylate embolization of angiographically occult pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysms.
articles.abstract: Angiographically occult pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysms - suspected on computed tomography but not shown at selective pulmonary angiography - have been presumed to have an occluded parent artery, and systemic-feeder embolization alone is often not curative. Three consecutive men with infection-related pseudoaneurysms presenting with massive hemoptysis were treated. In each, selective pulmonary angiography without occlusion showed proximal washout of injected contrast, consistent with reversed flow in the parent branch. The branch was occluded immediately proximal to the sac with a 4.0-mm microballoon - or, initially in one patient, a fortuitously wedged 5-F catheter - and hand injection under occlusion opacified the previously occult sac, which was then embolized with 25% n-butyl cyanoacrylate through a microballoon, without same-session systemic-artery embolization. All three achieved technical and clinical success, without recurrent hemoptysis over 17-22 months. Occultness does not equate to an occluded parent artery.

articles.title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biologic stent-graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for type 1 diabetes mellitus. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22 μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQ]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQ) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by ELISA. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling under idealized, non-physiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries. RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 ± 8 vs. 145 ± 20 μIU/mL under low vs. high glucose (p = 0.02), and secretion rates were 5,344 ± 144 vs. 6,795 ± 503 μIU/hr (p = 0.008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 ± 13 vs. 300 ± 17 μIU/mL (p = 0.014). CONCLUSION: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent-graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

articles.title: Patient-Defined Experience in Venous-Origin Chronic Pelvic Pain: Conceptual Foundation for a Disease-Specific Patient-Reported Outcome Measure.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the symptoms, daily life impacts, and patient-defined meaningful treatment benefits of women with venous-origin chronic pelvic pain (VO-CPP), and to establish the conceptual basis for a disease-specific patient-reported outcome measure (PROM). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-one adult women with gynecologic pain specialist-confirmed VO-CPP underwent semi-structured concept elicitation interviews at seven U.S. CENTERS: Interviews explored symptoms, daily life impacts, and patient-defined meaningful treatment benefits. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis to develop a patient-centered conceptual model. RESULTS: No new impact concepts emerged after five interviews and no new symptom concepts after sixteen; five additional interviews confirmed saturation of symptom and impact concepts. Participants reported a broad symptom burden, with 76% describing ≥10 symptoms, and all reported impacts across at least three daily life domains. Although pelvic pain reduction was the most frequently identified meaningful treatment benefit, participants consistently defined meaningful improvement as restoration of daily functioning and valued activities rather than pain reduction alone. CONCLUSION: Women with VO-CPP experience a multidimensional disease burden extending well beyond pain intensity alone. Treatment outcomes assessment should incorporate patient-defined symptoms, daily life impacts, and meaningful benefits. These findings provide a patient-centered conceptual foundation for development of a VO-CPP PROM.

articles.title: ReCo-Diff: residual-conditioned deterministic sampling for cold diffusion in sparse-view CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reduces radiation dose andacquisition time but introduces structured streak artifacts that make reconstructionseverely ill-posed. Cold-diffusion approaches can model such deterministic degradationprocesses, but existing sampling strategies may rely on scalar similarity criteria andpredefined thresholds to trigger sample-adaptive resets of the degradation-level trajectory.We aim to replace this threshold-based sampling control with spatially resolved residualconditioning. APPROACH: We propose ReCo-Diff, a residual-conditioned cold-diffusionframework for sparse-view CT reconstruction. At each reverse step, a zero-residualbaseline prediction is re-degraded using the CT degradation operator, and the resultingsigned image-domain re-degradation discrepancy is used as a spatial conditioning map fora second restoration pass. ReCo-Diff does not require an adaptive reset duringresidual-conditioned sampling and instead follows a predetermined degradation schedule.A one-time level transition is additionally used for highly sparse inputs. The method wasevaluated on the AAPM Low-Dose CT dataset under 18-, 36-, and 72-view settings using apatient-wise split with one held-out test volume. MAIN RESULTS: ReCo-Diff achievedPSNR values of 38.54, 42.57, and 46.98 dB at 18, 36, and 72 views, respectively. At 18views, matched-computation analysis showed that ReCo-Diff achieved 38.54 dB comparedwith 38.25 dB for a two-pass zero-residual control under the same 18-NFE budget. Aspatially shifted-residual control achieved 37.65 dB, indicating that effective residualconditioning benefits from spatial correspondence with the current degraded state.Significance. ReCo-Diff replaces adaptive trajectory control with step-wise spatialresidual conditioning in deterministic cold diffusion. Matched-computation analysis showsthat the reconstruction benefit depends on spatially aligned residual information ratherthan on the additional network evaluation alone. The proposed strategy provides analternative approach to controlling error propagation under a predetermined degradationschedule without relying on sample-adaptive reset decisions.

articles.title: DuDoTransGAN: Dual-Domain transformer based generative adversarial unsupervised network for metal artifact reduction in paired and unpaired CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Metal artifacts from implants degrade CT image quality, while supervised metal artifact reduction (MAR) methods require paired clean data that are rarely available clinically. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we developed DuDoTransGAN, an unsupervised dual-domain generative adversarial network for paired and unpaired training. It was evaluated on a publicly available paired synthetic dataset (SYN; 90,000 training and 2,000 test slices) and a clinical unpaired knee CT dataset (KNE; 19,032 slices from 66 patients; mean age, 55.8 ± 16.1 years; 36 males), including 6,168 slices with metal artifacts. On KNE, two radiologists independently assessed five image-quality aspects using Likert scales, with ratings reviewed by a senior radiologist. RESULTS: In the paired SYN experiment, DuDoTransGAN achieved a mean PSNR of 38.19 dB, the highest mean SSIM (0.975), and the lowest mean RMSE (5.65) among unsupervised methods. Performance remained stable with increasing metal-mask size, demonstrating robustness under larger-metal-mask conditions. In the unpaired KNE experiment, inter-rater agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.941). DuDoTransGAN achieved the highest mean scores among unsupervised methods for artifact removal (3.87 ± 0.48), diagnostic value (3.75 ± 0.50), visual effect (3.90 ± 0.36), and detail retention (3.96 ± 0.40), together with a comparable sharpness score (3.87 ± 0.58), and the highest radiologist selection rate (45 % vs 2 %-21 %). CONCLUSION: DuDoTransGAN is an adaptable unsupervised dual-domain MAR framework that performs effectively on paired synthetic and unpaired clinical data, producing high-quality, clinically interpretable CT images in the presence of metallic implants.

articles.title: Automated thigh muscle segmentation using foundation models: validation and impact of segmentation quality.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to validate a segmentation pipeline for the extraction of volumetric thigh muscle data, investigate the influence of demographics on segmentation performance, and investigate the influence of low-quality segmentations on quantitative performance and downstream metrics. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Manual thigh muscle segmentations on axial T1-weighted spin echo thigh images of 364 (106 training and validation; 258 testing) participants of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) were used. A trained YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection model generated labels and box predictions, that were passed to a fine-tuned foundation model (Segment Anything, Meta), which generated muscle segmentations. The quality of segmentations was assessed by two radiologists (none, minor, major issue), and Dice scores and mean bias versus manual segmentations were calculated in the testing dataset. Linear regression was used to calculate the associations of age, sex, and BMI with Dice scores. RESULTS: Dice scores ranged between 0.97 (quadriceps) and 0.89 (adductors). Exclusion of erroneous segmentations decreased mean bias by 0.06 mL across muscle groups; mean Dice of segmentations with versus without major issues was 0.90 versus 0.94. Female sex was associated with marginally lower Dice scores (beta -0.01, 95% CI: -0.02, -0.01, p < 0.001), while no other demographic feature showed significant associations. CONCLUSION: Foundation models can be fine-tuned on a modest task-specific dataset to achieve segmentation accuracy comparable to bespoke networks, without training a dedicated architecture from scratch. Visually erroneous segmentations introduce only negligible degradation of quantitative performance and downstream metrics and may thus be challenging to identify by data-driven detection strategies. KEY POINTS: Question Foundation models can be efficiently leveraged for robust segmentation on complex thigh muscle anatomy Findings Radiologist-identified erroneous segmentations introduced only negligible degradation of summary quantitative performance and are thus difficult to identify using statistical methods. Relevance statement Human-in-the-loop quality assurance post-validation adds limited value to improve downstream volumetric muscle metrics in foundation-model-based thigh segmentation. These findings carry implications for both research and potential clinical applications of muscle volume quantification, e.g., personalized therapeutic regimens.

articles.title: Interventional Radiology in Undergraduate Medical Education: A Kern's Framework Approach.
CDPDNet: Integrating text guidance with hybrid vision encoders for medical image segmentation.
articles.abstract: Most publicly available medical segmentation datasets are only partially labeled, with annotations provided for a subset of anatomical structures. When multiple datasets are combined for training, this incomplete annotation poses challenges, as it limits the model's ability to learn shared anatomical representations among datasets. Furthermore, vision-only frameworks often struggle to resolve semantic ambiguities between missing labels and target regions, potentially hindering discriminative performance and cross-dataset consistency. In this study, we proposed a CLIP-DINO Prompt-Driven Segmentation Network (CDPDNet), which combined a self-supervised vision transformer with CLIP-based text embedding and introduced task-specific text prompts to tackle these challenges. Specifically, the framework was constructed upon a convolutional neural network (CNN) and incorporated DINOv2 to extract both fine-grained and global visual features, which were then fused using a multi-head cross-attention module to overcome the limited long-range modeling capability of CNNs. In addition, CLIP-derived text embeddings were projected into the visual space to help model complex relationships among organs and tumors. To further address the partial label challenge and enhance inter-task discriminative capability, a Text-based Task Prompt Generation (TTPG) module that generated task-specific prompts was designed to guide the segmentation. Extensive experiments on multiple medical imaging datasets demonstrated that CDPDNet consistently outperformed existing state-of-the-art segmentation methods. Code and pretrained model are available at: https://github.com/wujiong-hub/CDPDNet.git.

articles.title: RADMorph: A region-aware deformable registration network for organ-specific thoracic CT alignment.
articles.abstract: Deformable image registration plays an important role in radiation therapy, supporting applications such as contour propagation, treatment planning, and motion analysis. However, accurate registration of lung CT images remains challenging in the presence of large respiratory-induced deformations. In this study, we propose RADMorph, a deep learning framework that explicitly models region-dependent motion to improve registration robustness and anatomical consistency under large deformations. RADMorph comprises two key components. The Adaptive Region Feature Encoder (ARFE) learns region-specific motion representations through feature clustering and region-conditioned filtering, while the Region-Centered Displacement Modulator (RCDM) estimates deformation fields by integrating local image similarity with inter-region distance-based modulation. We evaluated RADMorph on multi-center datasets acquired under free-breathing and deep-inspiration breath-hold conditions, as well as on four-dimensional CT datasets. Across these datasets, RADMorph showed competitive overall performance compared with convolutional and transformer-based registration methods, with improvements varying across geometric and intensity-based metrics. The proposed method improved contour propagation and boundary localization for clinically relevant structures in most evaluated settings while reducing global deformation folding. Quantitative evaluations further demonstrated accurate voxel-level correspondence across the evaluated datasets, supporting the potential use of RADMorph in applications that rely on spatial correspondence, such as dose mapping and adaptive radiotherapy. RADMorph integrates region-aware representation learning with distance-modulated deformation estimation to provide a region-informed approach for modeling complex respiratory motion. These characteristics may facilitate more reliable contour transfer and quantitative analysis of dynamic thoracic imaging.

articles.title: Upper Airway Muscle Stiffness in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Assessed by Shear Wave Elastography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: In obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), characterized by recurrent episodes of apnea and hypopnea, the activity of the upper airway dilator muscles is significant. In our study, we aimed to compare shear wave elastography (SWE) values of the genioglossus (GG), geniohyoid (GH), and mylohyoid (MH) muscles in patients with OSA. METHODS: In this prospective study, 90 adults who underwent full-night polysomnography were included. Participants were classified as non-OSA (apnea-hypopnea index [AHI] <5, n = 32) or OSA (AHI ≥5, n = 58), and OSA patients were further divided by severity. SWE was used to assess the stiffness of the bilateral GG, bilateral MH, and GH muscles. RESULTS: Bilateral GG and GH stiffness values were significantly higher in OSA patients than in non-OSA individuals, whereas bilateral MH measurements did not differ between groups (P < .001, .006, and .004, respectively). Among OSA subgroups, left GG stiffness was significantly higher in severe OSA than in mild-moderate OSA (P = .043). Right GG stiffness showed positive correlations with AHI and supine AHI (r = 0.392 and r = 0.491, respectively; both P < .001). Left GG stiffness was positively correlated with AHI and rapid eye movement-AHI (r = 0.338, P = .001; r = 0.423, P < .001). GH stiffness was positively correlated with both AHI and oxygen desaturation index (r = 0.313, P = .003; r = 0.302, P = .004). CONCLUSION: SWE may provide a useful non-invasive tool for evaluating upper airway muscle characteristics in OSA. Associations between upper airway muscle stiffness and polysomnographic parameters were observed; however, these cross-sectional findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating, requiring confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Comparison of two automated PGMI-based software tools for breast positioning quality assessment in DBT screening.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Automated "Perfect/Good/Moderate/Inadequate" (PGMI)-based tools have been developed to standardize breast positioning quality assessment, but their agreement remains uncertain. This study compared two automated software systems applied to the same digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) screening cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 778 women (3,112 views). Two software tools (SW1 and SW2) independently generated PGMI classifications and quality control (QC) feature outputs. Agreement was assessed using exact agreement and quadratic weighted κ. PGMI distributions were compared overall and by view, breast density, and breast volume. Associations between imaging parameters and PGMI scores were evaluated using Spearman correlation and ordinal regression. RESULTS: SW2 assigned more Inadequate ratings than SW1 (10.9% vs. 0.7%, p < 0.001), whereas SW1 assigned more Perfect (21.9% vs. 12.9%, p < 0.001). Overall agreement was limited (48.2%; κ = 0.044, 95% CI 0.006-0.085). Agreement was higher in mediolateral oblique than in craniocaudal views. Across SW1-derived density strata, SW2 assigned more Inadequate and fewer Perfect ratings in higher density strata, with smaller differences observed at higher breast volume. Higher volumetric breast density and breast thickness were associated with lower PGMI scores, whereas breast volume showed positive associations, with the effect more pronounced for SW2. QC patterns differed markedly: SW1 most frequently flagged inframammary fold and posterior positioning criteria, whereas SW2 identified pectoral muscle and parenchymal coverage issues. CONCLUSION: Two automated PGMI systems showed limited agreement and systematic differences in classification behavior. These findings indicate a lack of interchangeability and support the need for harmonized definitions and validation frameworks for automated image quality assessment. KEY POINTS: Question Standardized automated assessment of breast positioning quality in digital breast tomosynthesis remains lacking, limiting comparability between different PGMI-based software tools in screening. Findings Two automated PGMI systems showed limited agreement and systematic differences across views, breast density, breast volume, and acquisition-related parameters in DBT screening. Relevance statement Automated PGMI systems are not interchangeable and reflect different operational definitions of image quality. Harmonized standards and rigorous validation are required before implementation in clinical quality assurance workflows.

ACR TI-RADS Modified by CEUS Features and Nodule Location for Diagnosis and Biopsy Decision in Thyroid Nodules of TR4 or Higher.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop a modified American College of Radiology (ACR) thyroid imaging, reporting and data system (TI-RADS) incorporating contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) features and nodule location to improve diagnostic performance and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) recommendations for ACR TR4 or higher thyroid nodules. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent ultrasound and CEUS at 3 hospitals between June 2024 and January 2026. CEUS and location features were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression to construct the modified system. Diagnostic performance and biopsy recommendation efficiency were compared with ACR TI-RADS. RESULTS: Four hundred and eight patients with 442 nodules were included. Independent predictors included enhancement intensity, enhancement direction, ring enhancement, enhancement area and nodule location. In the training set (n = 334), the modified system achieved higher AUC and sensitivity than ACR TI-RADS (AUC: 0.90 [95% CI: 0.86-0.93] versus 0.75 [95% CI: 0.71-0.79]; sensitivity: 88.5% versus 60.3%; p < .01), higher accuracy of malignant nodule biopsies (AMB: 67.1% versus 49.4%), lower unnecessary biopsy rate (UBR: 32.9% versus 50.6%), and lower biopsy rate of benign nodules (BRB: 20.8% versus 31.2%), with no unsafe downgrading. Similar results were observed in the temporal validation set (n = 108): AUC 0.95 (95% CI: 0.90-0.99) versus 0.73 (95% CI: 0.66-0.79); sensitivity 87.0% versus 49.3%; AMB 83.3% versus 53.3%; UBR 16.7% versus 46.7%, and BRB 5.1% versus 17.9%. CONCLUSIONS: A modified ACR TI-RADS integrating CEUS features and nodule location improved diagnostic performance and FNA recommendations for ACR TR4 or higher nodules. Pending external validation, this system may provide a practical approach for refining risk stratification and reducing unnecessary biopsies.

articles.title: Incremental prognostic value of left atrial minimum volume index and late gadolinium enhancement in acute myocardial infarction patients with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤35.
articles.abstract: AIM: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤35% are at high risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). The left atrial minimum volume index (LAVImin) and late gadolinium enhancement of the left ventricular myocardium (LGE) have each been reported as stand-alone predictors, but their combined risk stratification and incremental prognostic value in this specific population remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-centre study included 338 patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% (training cohort, n = 235; external validation cohort, n = 103) imaged by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) between January 2014 and October 2024. Two blinded radiologists quantified LAVImin, LGE, and other CMR parameters. Cox regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis evaluated the separate and combined prognostic value of LAVImin and LGE. Five nested prediction models were developed and validated internally and externally. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 37 months, 55 of 235 training cohort patients (23.4%) experienced MACE. Patients with LAVImin ≥20.4 mL/m2 and LGE ≥29.5% had the poorest MACE-free survival (log-rank P < .001). The model combining clinical factors, conventional CMR risk factors, LAVImin and LGE (Model 5) discriminated best (apparent Harrell C statistic 0.77, optimism-corrected 0.73; external validation 0.78, calibration slope 0.96) and improved modestly but significantly on the conventional CMR model (Model 2; likelihood ratio P < .001, ΔAUC = 0.051, P = .04). CONCLUSION: In patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% who underwent CMR, combined LAVImin and LGE enable survival risk stratification and provide modest but significant incremental prognostic value for MACE.

articles.title: Machine learning for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and non-small cell lung cancer histological subtype classification: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: AIM: This study aimed to systematically review machine learning (ML) methods applied to computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)/CT for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and for lung cancer histological subtype classification. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched for original peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to May 31, 2026. Eligible studies applied ML, deep learning, or radiomics to CT, PET, or PET/CT for primary versus metastatic lung lesion differentiation or major lung cancer histological subtype classification. Methodological quality was assessed with Quality assessment of comparative diagnostic accuracy studies (QUADAS-2), and reporting was evaluated using 10 prespecified Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging-aligned items. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included after eligibility reassessment. Twenty-one provided a numeric study-level Area Under the Curve (AUC); the median representative AUC was 0.889 (IQR 0.820-0.936). The median AUC was 0.923 for primary/metastatic differentiation and 0.874 for histological subtype classification. Only 5 of 22 studies (22.7%) used independent external testing; among 4 externally validated studies with numeric AUCs, the median was 0.720. QUADAS-2 showed frequent uncertainty in patient selection (17/22, 77.3%), while CLAIM-aligned assessment identified limited external testing, code/model availability (3/22, 13.6%), and explainability reporting (4/22, 18.2%). CONCLUSION: CT- and PET/CT-based ML models show promising diagnostic performance for lung lesion-origin and histological subtype classification, but performance is lower in independent external evaluation. Broader multicentre validation, transparent reporting, reproducible code/model access, and prospective assessment are required before routine clinical implementation.
